fix: Set calc to false on far-int-01, -22, -25 and -26. Alternatively, add a second capitalizable cost to each, so the learner must add them.

issue: The internal-use software stage table puts 'data conversion' in the post-implementation/operation stage. Under ASC 350-40, data conversion usually happens during application development but is still expensed, as training is. A learner given 'data conversion during the application development stage' could wrongly capitalize it.
evidence: Lesson table row 3: 'Post-implementation / operation (training, maintenance, data conversion) | Expense'. ASC 350-40 requires data conversion costs (other than for software needed to convert data) to be expensed as incurred, even when they arise in application development, and ASC 350-40-55 describes them as typically incurred in that stage.
source: ASC 350-40-25 (data conversion and training costs); ASC 350-40-55
fix: Move data conversion out of the stage list. Add a line under the table: 'Training and data conversion are expensed whenever they occur, even during application development.'

issue: The lesson's citations list omits authorities the body relies on: ASC 350-40 (internal-use software and cloud-computing implementation costs; ASU 2018-15; ASU 2025-06), ASC 730 (R&D) and ASC 360-10 (impairment of finite-lived intangibles).
evidence: Frontmatter citations: 350-30, 350-20, 805-30-30-1, 720-15 only. The body cites ASC 730, ASC 360 and ASC 350-40 inline.
fix: Add 'FASB ASC 350-40 (Internal-use software; cloud computing arrangements)', 'FASB ASC 730-10 (Research and development)' and 'FASB ASC 360-10-35 (Impairment of long-lived assets)' to citations.

issue: Goodwill impairment and indefinite-lived intangible impairment are BAR content under the CPA Evolution Blueprints (carried into 2026), but most of this module's goodwill and indefinite-lived material is not marked optional. The P2-2 decision was also applied inconsistently. far-imp-04, -05 and -08 are optional, while far-imp-13, -14, -29 and -30 are the same goodwill computation and are not. As a result, BAR material counts toward FAR practice, readiness and the study plan, and the TBS scores three BAR cells.
evidence: Optional: far-imp-04 (goodwill cap), far-imp-05 (goodwill cap), far-imp-08 (PCC alternative). Not optional but the same BAR content: goodwill: far-imp-07 (testing order vs. goodwill), -13, -14, -29, -30 (cap computations), -15 (qualitative screen), -18 (annual test), -20 (interim trigger), fc4, fc6. Indefinite-lived intangibles: far-imp-03, -16, -23, -31, fc3. TBS rows loss.rl (radio license), loss.tn (trade name) and loss.gw (goodwill) are 3 of the 9 scored cells. The lesson states objective 2 as "Measure impairment for ... indefinite-lived intangibles, and goodwill" (task "Calculate goodwill and intangible asset impairment") and has full Indefinite-lived and Goodwill sections, with no scope note. Cross-module: far-int-16 (PCC goodwill alternative) is not optional, but its twin far-imp-08 is. Scope evidence: review/reference/far-standards.md §1c lists "Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangibles — No (BAR, per Becker)"; review/reference/blueprint-notes.md says FAR Area II F is "Finite-lived only: goodwill, indefinite-lived intangibles ... are BAR". Web search: SuperfastCPA files "Calculating Goodwill Impairment Losses" under BAR content area 2, Technical Accounting and Reporting (https://www.superfastcpa.com/?p=97096), and files FAR intangibles questions as "Carrying Amount of Finite-Lived Intangible Assets" (https://www.superfastcpa.com/?p=95014).
source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (eff. 1/1/2026): BAR Area II (indefinite-lived intangible assets, including goodwill); FAR Area II.F (intangible assets, finite-lived). REVIEW.md P2-2.
fix: Apply P2-2 consistently: mark far-imp-03, -07, -13, -14, -15, -16, -18, -20, -23, -29, -30, -31, fc3, fc4 and fc6 optional (and far-int-16 in far-intangibles). In the lesson, put the Indefinite-lived and Goodwill sections under a "BAR scope (optional for FAR)" callout, and reword objective 2 to cover held for sale only. In the TBS, replace the rl, tn and gw rows with FAR rows: a held-for-sale write-down, a finite-lived intangible tested under ASC 360, and next-year depreciation on the new cost basis. A TBS cannot be partly optional. If the team instead confirms that goodwill is FAR, unmark far-imp-04, -05 and -08 and remove the P2-2 entry. Either way, keep the flags consistent.

issue: Two pure-recall items are labeled skill "analysis" and difficulty 3. That is two skill levels too high, and it inflates the module's analysis count, which feeds the Blueprint skill-mix targets.
evidence: far-imp-27: "An impaired asset held and used recovers in fair value the next year. What happens?" The key is "No reversal", which recalls one rule (ASC 360-10-35-20) and is also tested by far-imp-11 (remembering/1). far-imp-21: "A company plans to abandon a machine in 6 months. How is it accounted for?" The key is "As held and used", which recalls one rule (ASC 360-10-45-15). Neither stem gives data to examine or interrelate. Both are labeled analysis/3.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions (Remembering and Understanding vs. Analysis); src/content/schema.ts skill and difficulty fields
fix: Relabel both remembering, difficulty 1. Alternatively, rewrite them as real analysis items: for example, give a machine to be abandoned with its cost, prior depreciation and revised life, and ask for current-year depreciation and the classification.

issue: Skill and difficulty labels are off by one level. Items 22-31 are uniformly labeled analysis/3, but each is a single application of one formula. Items 19, 20 and 23 are pure recall labeled application. The same computation is labeled differently in two places.
evidence: Application labeled analysis/3: 22 (900/950/700, UCF > CA so 0), 24 (500-380 = 120,000), 25 (520 > 500 so 0), 26 (300-(280-15) = 35,000), 28 (min(50,35) = 35,000), 29 (min(100,200) = 100,000), 30 (min(100,50) = 50,000), 31 (200-170 = 30,000, trivial at difficulty 3). Recall labeled application: 19 (finite-lived intangibles use recoverability then fair value), 20 (a major adverse change is a trigger), 23 (the qualitative screen exists). Inconsistent: far-x2-10 has the same numbers as far-imp-24 and is labeled application/2, but 24 is analysis/3. cues.md reports 11 analysis labels among 33 practice and exam items. After relabeling, the module has no genuine analysis-level item, against the FAR target of 35-45%.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel 22, 24, 25, 26, 28, 29 and 30 as application, difficulty 2; 31 as application, difficulty 1; and 19, 20 and 23 as remembering. To keep analysis coverage, add 2-3 real analysis items. Examples: identify the asset group from cash-flow interdependence; choose among held-for-sale, held-and-used and abandoned with multi-period effects; reconcile a fixed-asset schedule after an impairment.

issue: The explanations do not teach. Many distractor explanations are just "Not the computation." and never say which error produces the number. The item-level explanations state the rule but show no computation.
evidence: Each "Not the computation." distractor and the error that actually produces it (reproduced in python): 22(b) 250,000 = UCF 950,000 - FV 700,000; 24(c) 70,000 = UCF 450,000 - FV 380,000; 25(c) 20,000 = UCF - CA; 25(d) 140,000 = UCF 520,000 - FV 380,000; 26(b) 15,000 = costs to sell only; 28(d) 15,000 = 50,000 - 35,000 (the recovery above the cap); 29(d) 300,000 = excess 100,000 + goodwill 200,000; 30(d) 150,000 = excess + goodwill; 31(b) 170,000 = fair value as the loss; 31(c) 200,000 = full write-off. Item-level explanations without numbers: 13 ("goodwill impairment = CA - FV, not exceeding goodwill"), 14, 17 ("allocate pro rata", with no 300/500 x 100 = 60,000), 22, 24, 25, 26 (no 280 - 15 = 265), 28, 29, 30, 31. Compare far-imp-03, -05 and far-x2-10, which show the full computation.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 4 (explanations state the rule and show the computation)
fix: Replace each "Not the computation." with the error it models, for example 24(c): "70,000 subtracts fair value from undiscounted cash flows; those cash flows only test recoverability." Rewrite each item-level explanation to show the steps, for example 26: "FV less cost to sell = 280,000 - 15,000 = 265,000; loss = 300,000 - 265,000 = 35,000."

issue: Distractor (d) $200,000 is labeled outdated-rule, and its explanation blames the old implied-goodwill Step 2. Step 2 cannot produce $200,000 from this stem, so the rationale names an error that does not generate the number.
evidence: The stem gives a carrying amount of 5,000,000 (goodwill 800,000) and a fair value of 4,600,000. Pre-ASU 2017-04 Step 2 needs the fair value of the unit's identifiable net assets, which the stem does not give. Using carrying amounts as a proxy, implied goodwill = 4,600,000 - 4,200,000 = 400,000 and the loss = 800,000 - 400,000 = 400,000, which is the key. No rule-based error gives 200,000.
source: ASC 350-20-35-8 (as amended by ASU 2017-04)
fix: Add "the fair value of the unit's identifiable net assets is $4,400,000" to the stem and change (d) to $600,000 (old Step 2: implied goodwill 200,000; 800,000 - 200,000 = 600,000), keeping outdated-rule. Alternatively, change (d) to $1,200,000 (excess + goodwill) with trap wrong-rule.

issue: Some trap labels do not match the misconception the distractor models, and the same error is labeled differently from item to item.
evidence: 05(c) 300,000 = excess 1,200,000 - goodwill 900,000 is labeled "reversed"; the same error is "wrong-rule" in 14(b) and 04(c). 24(b) 50,000 and x2-10(a) 50,000 (CA - UCF, the recoverability gap) are labeled "wrong-rule"; the same error is "partial-computation" in chk1(a), 09(b) and x2-29(a). 18(a) "Only when a triggering event occurs" and 23(c) "Only for goodwill, not intangibles" are labeled "partial-computation" on non-numeric items; they model incomplete-rule or scope errors (wrong-rule or wrong-classification).
source: src/content/schema.ts TRAP_TYPES
fix: 05(c) -> wrong-rule; 24(b) and x2-10(a) -> partial-computation; 18(a) -> wrong-rule; 23(c) -> wrong-classification.

issue: Answer cues: in each item the key is the only qualified, hedged option and is much longer than the others, while the distractors are bare or absolute.
evidence: chk2: the key is "A held-for-sale asset, up to prior losses", the only option with a qualifier. The others are bare asset names ("Goodwill of a reporting unit", "A factory held and used", "An indefinite-lived trademark"). 18: the key is "At least annually, and between tests if triggered". The distractors are "Only when a triggering event occurs", "Every three years" and "Only when the business is sold", with absolutes in (a) and (d). cues.md flags both items as "key much longest".
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 6
fix: chk2: give the distractors parallel qualifiers ("Goodwill, up to the original balance", "A factory held and used, up to the prior loss", "An indefinite-lived trademark, through OCI"). 18: use parallel-length options, such as "Annually only, on a fixed date", "Only when a triggering event occurs, at the entity level", "At least annually, and between tests if triggered" and "Every three years, unless triggered sooner".

issue: Several distractors are implausible, or do not answer the question asked, so these items test elimination rather than knowledge.
evidence: 01(b) "A routine increase in accumulated depreciation" and (c) "Payment of a regular dividend". 20(c) "Paying a regular dividend" (the dividend filler again) and (d) "A 2% rise in quarterly revenue". 19(c) "It's never tested". 23(b) "Yes, always, with no assessment". 16(d) "Amortization of $90,000" answers a different question; the stem asks for the impairment loss.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ checks 2 and 8
fix: Use near-miss distractors from the indicator and qualitative-factor lists. For 01: "A current-period operating loss with no history of losses" (not by itself an indicator), or "A decline in fair value that is below carrying amount but above undiscounted cash flows" (an indicator only if significant). For 20: "A decline in the entity's share price that is not sustained". For 19: "Annual qualitative screen, then fair value only". For 23: "Yes, but only if the asset was acquired within the past year". For 16: "$950,000 write-up to fair value".

issue: Redundancy: the held-and-used two-step test is asked 8 times in the same form (pre1, chk1, 09, 22, 24, 25, x2-10, x2-29), plus the lesson's worked example and TBS rows eq and bl. far-imp-22 reuses the lesson's trap numbers verbatim, and far-imp-25 is far-imp-24 with only the undiscounted cash flows changed. Both reward memorizing numbers.
evidence: Lesson trap: "if undiscounted cash flows had been $950,000, there is no impairment", with CA 900,000 and FV 700,000. far-imp-22: CA 900,000, UCF 950,000, FV 700,000, key $0, identical. far-imp-24: 500,000/450,000/380,000, key 120,000. far-imp-25: 500,000/520,000/380,000, key 0; cues.md gives Jaccard 0.82. pre1 (500,000/540,000/420,000, key 0) already tests the "recoverable despite a lower FV" trap. That makes 3 items (pre1, 22, 25) that test that one trap with near-identical structure.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7
fix: Rewrite 22 and 25 to test untested ASC 360 rules: (i) next-year depreciation on the new cost basis (e.g., new basis 700,000 / 5 remaining years = 140,000); (ii) cash-flow horizon based on the remaining life of the primary asset; (iii) an impairment indicator present but the asset recoverable, followed by a revision of useful life. Keep pre1 as the trap item.

issue: The mock-exam item far-x2-10 is a clone of practice item far-imp-24: same facts, same numbers, same key and the same distractor amounts. A learner who has practiced sees an item already answered, which inflates the mock score as a readiness signal.
evidence: far-imp-24: "Equipment held and used has a $500,000 carrying amount, $450,000 of undiscounted cash flows and a $380,000 fair value", options 120,000/50,000/70,000/0, key 120,000. far-x2-10: "An asset group held and used has a carrying amount of $500,000, undiscounted future cash flows of $450,000, and a fair value of $380,000", options 50,000/0/70,000/120,000, key 120,000. The cross-bank finding F-0188 (S2) also flags this pair.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7; F-0188
fix: Rewrite far-x2-10 with new numbers and a twist not drilled in practice. Example: an asset group with a $10,000 selling-cost distractor and a PV figure, CA 640,000, UCF 610,000, FV 520,000, PV 540,000, key 120,000. Alternatively, retire far-imp-24.

issue: Redundancy: "goodwill loss = reporting-unit CA - FV, capped at goodwill" is asked 6 times in this module in the same form, in two mirrored pairs (13/14 and 29/30), plus the lesson's faded example (3 steps), TBS row gw and far-x2-11.
evidence: Excess below goodwill: 04 (1.5M < 2.0M), 13 (400,000 < 800,000), 29 (100,000 < 200,000). Excess above goodwill, capped: 05 (1.2M -> 900,000), 14 (1.0M -> 800,000), 30 (100,000 -> 50,000). 13 and 14 share the stem and differ only in FV (Jaccard 0.76); 29 and 30 differ only in goodwill (0.87). The cross-bank finding F-0197 also flags this cluster.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7; F-0197
fix: Keep one below-cap item (04) and one capped item (05). Retire 13, 14, 29 and 30, or rewrite them to test other goodwill rules if goodwill stays in scope (for example, the testing order with an asset-group impairment that changes the RU carrying amount). Under M-far-impairment-001 (BAR scope) these are and optional anyway.

issue: Redundancy: far-imp-11 and far-imp-27 test the identical fact ("no reversal of a held-and-used impairment") in the same way. The same rule is also the answer to chk2's option (b), far-imp-02's option (d) and fc5.
evidence: 11: "Under U.S. GAAP, may an impairment loss on an asset held and used be reversed if its fair value later recovers?", key "No". 27: "An impaired asset held and used recovers in fair value the next year. What happens?", key "No reversal". Both have reversal-up-to-the-loss and OCI distractors.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7; ASC 360-10-35-20
fix: Rewrite 27 as an application item. Example: equipment written down to 700,000 with 5 years remaining; next year its fair value rises to 800,000; ask for the carrying amount at the end of that year (700,000 - 140,000 = 560,000; no write-up).

issue: Lesson-item alignment: two practice items test rules the lesson never teaches. Held for sale, which four items compute with, gets no body section, only a flowchart box, one takeaway and a table row.
evidence: far-imp-17 tests pro-rata allocation of an asset-group loss by carrying amount, with no asset reduced below its determinable fair value (ASC 360-10-35-28). The lesson never mentions allocation, and the "asset group" concept (lowest level of largely independent cash flows, 360-10-35-23) is not defined. far-imp-21 tests that an asset to be abandoned stays held and used until abandoned, with depreciation revised (360-10-45-15, 360-10-35-47); the lesson does not mention abandonment. Held for sale: far-imp-06, -12, -26 and -28 require FV less cost to sell, no depreciation, and recovery limited to cumulative losses. The lesson gives these only as one-line rules, with no worked example and no classification criteria (360-10-45-9).
fix: Add a short "Held for sale" body section with the classification criteria and a worked example (write-down to FV less cost to sell, then a recovery capped at prior losses). Add 2-3 sentences on asset groups and pro-rata allocation (with the fair-value floor), and one sentence on assets to be abandoned (held and used until abandoned; revise depreciation).

issue: The lesson presents the one-step goodwill test as a public-entity rule: "For public business entities (ASU 2017-04)", the takeaway "Goodwill (public entities)" and fc4 "(public, ASU 2017-04)". ASU 2017-04 removed Step 2 for all entities. A private company that does not elect the PCC alternative uses the same one-step test, which the lesson leaves unclear.
evidence: ASU 2017-04 was effective for SEC filers for FY beginning after 12/15/2019 and for all other entities for FY beginning after 12/15/2022. It now applies to every entity that applies ASC 350-20 without the alternative. The lesson contrasts "public" only with "private companies may elect to amortize", which implies non-electing private companies follow some other model.
source: ASC 350-20-35-8 (ASU 2017-04); ASC 350-20-35-62 to 35-82 (accounting alternative)
fix: Reword to "All entities (ASU 2017-04), unless a private company or NFP elects the goodwill alternative". Update the takeaway and fc4 to match.

issue: The lesson says "(IFRS permits reversals for assets other than goodwill — a common comparison question.)" IFRS-versus-U.S. GAAP differences have not been tested on FAR since the July 2021 Blueprint, so calling this "a common comparison question" for the 2026 exam is outdated.
evidence: Journal of Accountancy (Nov 2020) on the post-practice-analysis Blueprint: candidates "no longer will be tested on the differences between IFRS and U.S. GAAP" (https://www.journalofaccountancy.com/news/2020/nov/cpa-exam-refresh-after-practice-analysis/). Surgent lists the IFRS differences among FAR content removed in July 2021 (https://www.surgent.com/blog/cpa_exam_changes_2021/). The reference sheet (far-standards.md §1c) also says IFRS is "believed not tested".
source: AICPA Blueprint (July 2021 onward) as reported by the Journal of Accountancy and Surgent
fix: Delete the sentence, or reword it as "(For background only: IFRS permits reversals other than for goodwill; IFRS is not tested on the 2026 CPA Exam.)"

issue: Sequencing: far-impairment comes before far-intangibles in far.yaml, but the lesson and its items assume the learner already knows what goodwill, reporting units and indefinite-lived (versus finite-lived) intangibles are. Those are introduced only in the next module, and the intangibles lesson points back ("tested for impairment (see the impairment module)").
evidence: far.yaml u6 order: far-ppe-acquisition, far-depreciation, far-impairment, far-intangibles. The impairment lesson never defines goodwill, a reporting unit or an indefinite life. far-imp-03, -16, -19, -23, -31 and all the goodwill items depend on them. The far-intangibles lesson defines the finite/indefinite split and goodwill measurement.
source: content/sections/far.yaml; content/far/modules/far-intangibles/lesson.md
fix: Either move far-impairment after far-intangibles in far.yaml, or add a 3-line primer at the top of the impairment lesson (goodwill = residual in an acquisition; reporting unit; indefinite-lived = no foreseeable limit to its cash flows) with a link to far-intangibles.

issue: The research part is not discriminating: each wrong excerpt covers a different asset class (indefinite-lived intangibles, goodwill, held for sale), so a candidate can eliminate them from the asset type alone, without reading the guidance.
evidence: The prompt asks why the held-and-used studio building is not impaired. Excerpts (a) 350-30, (c) 350-20 and (d) 360-10-35-43 (held for sale) cannot apply to a held-and-used building. Only (b) 360-10-35-17 is about held-and-used assets. The key is correct.
fix: Replace two distractors with near-miss held-and-used excerpts, such as 360-10-35-21 (indicators that trigger a test) and 360-10-35-20 (new cost basis; no restoration), so the candidate must distinguish the recoverability rule from related ASC 360 paragraphs.

issue: Option (d) is the text "$     0" (padded with spaces). HTML collapses whitespace, so it will render as "$ 0", which looks like a typo. It is also inconsistent with the "None ($0)" wording in far-x2-10 and the practice items.
evidence: far-exam-area2.json: "text": "$     0". The same padding appears in two other exam items in the area 1 and area 2 files.
fix: Change it to "None ($0)" or "$0".

issue: The stem says the asset's "fair value later rises by $50,000". The held-for-sale gain is measured on the increase in fair value less cost to sell (ASC 360-10-35-40). The key holds only if costs to sell are unchanged.
evidence: Key (a) 35,000 = min(50,000 increase, 35,000 cumulative loss). If costs to sell had also changed, the recognized increase would differ. The stem is silent on this.
fix: Reword to "...was written down by $35,000 to fair value less cost to sell; fair value less cost to sell later rises by $50,000."

issue: Explanation presents SAS 149 (revised AU-C 600) as the governing standard and the stem uses its term 'component performance materiality', but SAS 149 is not testable on the 2026 exam; the stem also compares component PM with group *materiality* while the explanation compares it with group *performance materiality*.
evidence: SAS 149 is effective for audits of group FS for periods ending on or after Dec 15, 2026 (reference sheet §2, verified); under the AICPA eligibility rule (later of first quarter after earliest mandatory effective date / first quarter beginning 6 months after issuance) it is testable from Jan 1, 2027 (reference sheet §1 test-date map). The 2026 exam tests extant AU-C 600, whose rule is that component materiality is lower than materiality for the group FS as a whole (AU-C 600.22, from memory). The aud-using-others lesson itself labels the SAS 149 terminology as applying to periods ending on or after Dec 15, 2026. Stem: 'component performance materiality ... relate to group materiality'; explanation: '...lower than group performance materiality'. Key 'lower' is the same under both versions, so the key survives; the authority and terms do not.
source: AU-C 600.22 (extant, pre-SAS 149); SAS 149 effective date; AICPA CPA Exam policy on new pronouncements
fix: Rewrite to the 2026-testable rule: stem 'In a group audit under AU-C 600, how should component materiality relate to group materiality?'; explanation 'AU-C 600: component materiality is set lower than materiality for the group financial statements as a whole, to reduce aggregation risk. (SAS 149, testable from 2027, uses component performance materiality set lower than group performance materiality.)' Fix choice d's explanation to the same term.

issue: Skill labels are two levels too high: aud-pl-15 (analysis) asks for recall of a single rule ('lower'); aud-pl-27 (evaluation) asks for recall of the AU-C 450.08 response to misstatements approaching materiality.
evidence: aud-pl-15: no data or relationships to examine; the answer is the recalled rule 'component materiality is lower than group materiality' = Remembering & Understanding (analysis is two levels up). aud-pl-27: one-line stem, the key 'Do added procedures' restates AU-C 450.08 (revise strategy/plan when aggregate misstatements approach materiality); the distractors (stop accumulating, raise materiality, adverse opinion now) need no weighing of evidence = Application at most (evaluation is two levels up). These inflate the module's analysis/evaluation share (labelled mix of practice+exam: R 39%, Ap 21%, An 33%, E 6%; Blueprint R 30-40, Ap 30-40, An 15-25, E 5-15).
source: AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint skill definitions; AU-C 450.08; AU-C 600.22
fix: aud-pl-15 → skill remembering, difficulty 1-2. aud-pl-27 → skill application, difficulty 2; or rewrite pl-27 as a real evaluation item (give accumulated misstatements, materiality, remaining untested populations and ask which response is best).

issue: Skill and/or difficulty labels are one level off.
evidence: aud-pl-16 'What does the detailed audit plan describe?', aud-pl-17 'what must the auditor obtain about opening balances?' and aud-pl-18 'Why might the auditor perform some substantive procedures at an interim date?' are recall items labelled application (→ remembering). aud-pl-20 (1,000,000 × 1.05 × 1.03 = 1,081,500) is a one-step calculation labelled analysis (→ application). aud-pl-24 (2,000,000 × 5% = 100,000, rate given) is labelled analysis, difficulty 3 (→ application, difficulty 1). aud-pl-26 (benchmark fell from 2,000,000 to 1,200,000 → lower materiality) is a one-step directional rule labelled evaluation, difficulty 3 (→ application/analysis, difficulty 2).
source: AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint skill definitions
fix: Relabel: pl-16/17/18 remembering; pl-20 application; pl-24 application, difficulty 1; pl-26 analysis (or application), difficulty 2.

issue: calc: true is set on items whose key needs no computation.
evidence: aud-pl-08: any expected increase vs. a flat balance leads to the key 'investigate'; the 13.3% figure only appears in the explanation. aud-pl-26: the key 'Lower materiality' follows from the direction of the benchmark change; no amount is asked for (contrast aud-rm-14, which asks for the revised $60,000).
source: src/content/schema.ts (calc = item requires a computation)
fix: Set calc: false on aud-pl-08 and aud-pl-26, or make them computational (e.g., pl-26 ask for the revised materiality at 5%: $60,000).

issue: Stem says payroll was expected to rise 'about 10%' because headcount grew 10% and wages rose 3%; those drivers give about 13%, which is what the explanation states. Distractor (c) 'because it should have fallen' contradicts the stem's own expectation of a rise.
evidence: 1.10 × 1.03 = 1.133 → +13.3% (python). Explanation: 'Expected ≈ +13% (1.10 × 1.03 = 1.133)'. The adjacent item aud-pl-20 teaches exactly this compounding, so the stem's 10% reads as an error.
source: Arithmetic
fix: Change the stem to 'expected payroll expense to rise about 13%'; rewrite (c) as 'Payroll must be overstated, because a flat balance means no change occurred' or another plausible wrong conclusion.

issue: Distractor rationales do not describe the errors that produce the numbers: (c) 40 days is said to use 'the wrong daily sales figure' but no figure in the stem yields it; (d) 73 days is said to 'invert the computation' (trap reversed), but inverting gives 7.3 (choice b) or 0.02.
evidence: python: 750,000 ÷ (5,475,000 ÷ 365) = 50.0; 5,475,000 ÷ 750,000 = 7.3 (turnover, choice b, correctly explained); 40 days would need daily sales of 18,750 (annual 6,843,750), which is not in the stem; 73 = 5,475,000 ÷ 75,000 (a decimal slip) or 7.3 × 10 — not an inversion.
source: Arithmetic
fix: Replace (c) and (d) with reproducible errors and matching labels, e.g., 49.3 days (360-day year: 750,000 ÷ (5,475,000 ÷ 360); trap wrong-rule) and 0.14 years / or 136.9 days; or keep 73 and explain it as 5,475,000 ÷ 75,000 (misplaced decimal, trap distractor-number).

issue: Trap label 'partial-computation' is used for distractors on non-computational items, where the misconception is an incomplete or overly narrow rule.
evidence: pl-01 (a) 'Only at the overall review stage'; pl-11 (a) 'Understated cost of goods sold only'; pl-12 (b) 'Presentation of receivables only'; pl-16 (c) 'Only the audit budget and fee'; pl-17 (d) 'Only management's representations'; pl-19 (c) 'Only inventory understatement'. issue: Answer cues: the key is the only hedged option against absolute distractors, or distractors overlap/duplicate each other so they can be eliminated without the rule.
evidence: pl-01: (a) 'Only…', (b) 'Only…', (c) 'At all three stages' vs key (d) unqualified. pl-08: (a) 'No risk exists', (c) 'must', (d) 'can't… every' vs key 'possible misstatement'. x2-02: (a) 'No risk', (c) 'must be understated' vs key 'possible misstatement'. pl-19: (c) 'Only inventory understatement' is a subset of key (d) 'COGS overstated…' (understated ending inventory overstates COGS) — overlapping options. pl-26: (a) 'Keep the original amount' and (d) 'Ignore the change' are the same answer, so both fall together.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 6
fix: Give each item at least one hedged, plausible distractor (e.g., pl-08 'The difference is explained by the wage increase, so no work is needed'; x2-02 'The margin is plausible because volume rose'); replace pl-19 (c) with 'Ending inventory overstated' (which would raise, not lower, the margin); replace pl-26 (d) with 'Keep materiality but lower performance materiality only'.

issue: Implausible distractors make these items near-giveaways, inconsistent with their difficulty labels (pl-25 and x2-04 are the only reasonable choice at a glance).
evidence: pl-09: cash balance / number of shareholders / total assets as a room-revenue expectation. pl-14: 'rely without testing', 'exclude the derivatives', 'issue a disclaimer immediately'. pl-25 (analysis, difficulty 3): 'Better controls', 'Lower fraud risk', 'Normal variation' for a 30%→42% margin jump with no business change. x2-04: 'It must exclude the engagement partner'.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 2 and 8
fix: Use CPA-style plausible alternatives: pl-09 'Last year's room revenue adjusted for CPI'; pl-14 'Use the client's valuation specialist's report as audit evidence without evaluating it' / 'Plan to rely on management's representation'; pl-25 'A favourable sales-mix shift' as a plausible-but-unsupported option; x2-04 'It is held once, at the start, and need not be revisited'. Or lower pl-25 to difficulty 1.

issue: Seven of the 27 practice items (26%) test content the aud-planning lesson never teaches and that is taught only in later modules, so learners meet them untaught and misses route back to a lesson that cannot help.
evidence: Lesson body and takeaways contain no materiality, performance materiality, component/group materiality, misstatement accumulation or interim-testing content (grep). Materiality items pl-21, 22, 24, 26 and AU-C 450 item pl-27 belong to aud-risk-materiality (the next module, aud-u3); group-audit item pl-15 to aud-using-others (aud-u8, AUD-III); interim substantive testing pl-18 to aud-risk-response (aud-u5, whose lesson teaches it at lines 86-88). aud-pl-17 (AU-C 510) is at least taught in the earlier aud-engagement-acceptance module.

fix: Move pl-15 to aud-using-others, pl-18 to aud-risk-response and pl-21/22/24/26/27 to aud-risk-materiality (or delete those that duplicate aud-rm items — see the duplication finding), and replace them with planning items the lesson supports: strategy-vs-plan classification scenarios, analytics with nonfinancial drivers, absence-of-expected-change cases, TCWG planning communication, team discussion content.

issue: Redundancy: the single fact 'strategy = scope, timing, direction; plan = nature, timing, extent' is tested by seven MCQs (plus pre1, chk1 and flashcard f1), several as mirror images; mock item x2-01 reuses chk1's distractor almost verbatim.
evidence: pl-13 'Which element sets the scope, timing and direction?' → strategy; pl-23 'What does the overall audit strategy set?' → scope, timing and direction (exact reverse). pl-16 'What does the detailed audit plan describe?' → NTE; x2-36 'part of the detailed plan rather than the strategy' → NTE. x2-01 (b) 'Selecting the specific invoices to vouch for sales cutoff testing' ≈ chk1 (b) 'The specific invoices to vouch for sales cut-off'. Same fact, same way, >3 times.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7
fix: Keep pl-13 and x2-36; replace pl-16 and pl-23 with application items (e.g., which change requires updating the overall strategy vs. only the plan; planning direction, supervision and review; initial-engagement planning under AU-C 300.13); give x2-01 new distractors not used in the lesson check.

issue: Cross-module near-duplicates: these practice items repeat items in other modules, in two cases with identical numbers.
evidence: pl-26 ($2,000,000 planned → $1,200,000 actual pretax income; lower materiality) ≈ aud-rm-14 (same $2,000,000 / $1,200,000, key 'Revise it to $60,000') and aud-rm-07. pl-11 'Inventory turnover fell from 8 times to 5 times while sales were stable' ≈ aud-inv-24 'Inventory turnover fell from 8 to 5 while sales stayed flat' (same key). pl-24 (5% × $2,000,000) ≈ mock item aud-x2-25 (same 5% × $2,000,000 base) and aud-rm-05. pl-21 ≈ aud-rm-04 (pretax income benchmark). pl-22 ≈ aud-rm-16 and aud-rm-chk2 (PM lower than materiality).
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7
fix: Delete pl-21, pl-22, pl-24 and pl-26 (aud-risk-materiality already covers them) and rewrite pl-11 with different facts (e.g., DSI, or turnover falling while sales rose) or drop it.

issue: Mock-exam duplication: aud-x2-04 and aud-x2-46 (aud-understanding-entity) sit in the same testlet of aud-mock-3 and test the same fact with the same key; aud-x2-39 on aud-mock-3 is a near-verbatim copy of the lesson check aud-pl-chk2.
evidence: aud-mock-3 testlet 2 contains both aud-x2-46 ('…engagement team discussion… correct?' key 'It covers how fraud might occur in the statements') and aud-x2-04 ('…engagement team discussion is correct?' key 'It should cover how fraud could occur in the statements'). aud-x2-39 ('Which procedure is not a risk assessment procedure?' options inquiry / analytics / observation-inspection / confirming AR, key d) = aud-pl-chk2 options and key. One mock item reveals the other; the mock rewards memory of the lesson check.

fix: Replace aud-x2-04 on aud-mock-3 (or rewrite it to test another aspect, e.g., who must participate or when the discussion is revisited); rewrite aud-pl-chk2 with different procedures (e.g., 'reading minutes vs. recomputing depreciation') so the mock item is not pre-exposed.

issue: This substantive-analytical-procedure TBS is mapped to aud-planning (unit aud-u3, AUD-II), but substantive analytics (expectation, threshold, investigate the difference) are AUD-III content taught in aud-data-analytics and aud-risk-response; the aud-planning lesson only says substantive analytics are optional.
evidence: TBS title 'Substantive analytical procedures'; moduleIds ['aud-planning'], unitId aud-u3. The threshold/investigation steps are taught in aud-data-analytics lesson lines 111-114 and aud-risk-response (rr-chk2, rr-10, rr-13, rr-18). aud-planning lesson never mentions thresholds. Coverage counts this TBS under AUD-II, and misses route to a lesson that does not teach it.
source: AU-C 520.05; content/sections/aud.yaml
fix: Change moduleIds to ['aud-data-analytics'] (unitId aud-u6) or ['aud-risk-response'] (aud-u5).

issue: Skill and time are overstated: the task is three one-step multiplications, three subtractions and three threshold comparisons (labelled analysis, 20 minutes).
evidence: ie 8,000,000 × 6% = 480,000; pe 120 × 55,000 = 6,600,000; de 12,000,000 ÷ 10 = 1,200,000; differences 60,000 / 50,000 / 300,000 vs. thresholds 25,000 / 100,000 / 60,000. No explanations to evaluate, no precision or data-reliability judgment. Realistic time ≈ 8-10 minutes; skill = application ('perform substantive analytical procedures').
source: AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint skill definitions; AU-C 520.05
fix: Relabel skill application and minutes 10, or add analysis rows (e.g., management's explanation of the interest difference — a mid-year $1M drawdown — to corroborate; whether to investigate the whole difference or the excess; expectation precision).

issue: The dropdown part's row labels give away the numeric part's answers (gross margin 36%, allowance 2%, days in inventory 91).
evidence: Row k1 'Gross margin rose to 36%…' = gm key 36.0; k2 'allowance fell from 5% to 2%…' = alw key 2.0; k3 'Days in inventory rose from 73 to 91 days' ≈ dsi key 91.3. Both parts are in one simulation, so a candidate can copy three of the four numeric answers.
source: Review brief §2 per-TBS checks (exhibits/answers consistent; no cues)
fix: Make the risk rows qualitative ('The gross margin movement compared with the industry', 'The allowance coverage trend', 'The days-in-inventory trend'), or show the numeric results only after part r is submitted.

issue: Row k1 (margin up to 36%): 'Inventory — valuation' is a plausible competing answer that the explanation does not address; the exhibit's clean 'inventory costing' test does not clearly cover lower-of-cost-and-NRV, and k3 shows slow-moving stock.
evidence: An unrecorded obsolescence write-down understates cost of sales and inflates margin. Size check (python): to lift margin from 30% to 36% on 9,125,000 sales, COGS would have to be understated by 547,500 = 37.5% of year-end inventory 1,460,000 — implausible as a missed write-down, whereas fictitious sales of ~782,000 explain both the margin and DSO 40→60. So Revenue — occurrence is best, but the explanation only rules out 'Cost of sales — completeness'.
source: AU-C 315 (risk identification from analytics); ASC 330-10-35
fix: Add a sentence to k1's explanation: 'A missed inventory write-down would also lift the margin, but it would need to be about $548,000 (37.5% of inventory), and the receivables build-up points to revenue.' Optionally say in the exhibit that the NRV review is not yet done (which keeps k3 = valuation).

issue: Worked example 'Scanning the ratios' compares a Year 2 inventory turnover on average inventory (3.6) with a Year 1 turnover on year-end inventory (4.0), teaching an inconsistent comparison.
evidence: python: Y2 2,847,000 ÷ 800,000 avg = 3.56; Y1 2,810,500 ÷ 700,000 year-end = 4.02; like-for-like Y2 on year-end inventory 2,847,000 ÷ 900,000 = 3.16. Every other worked number checks: GM 35.0% vs 30.0%; DSO 50.0 vs 36.4 days; faded block 20,000 / 50 / 30 days.
source: Arithmetic
fix: Compute both years on year-end inventory (3.2 vs 4.0 times) — matching aud-tbs-u3-analytics, which uses year-end inventory — and drop the 'Year 1 average not available' caveat.

issue: The lesson says only the audit plan is updated during the audit; AU-C 300 requires updating both the overall strategy and the plan (and item aud-pl-10 keys 'revise the strategy and plan').
evidence: Takeaway: 'The plan is more detailed and is updated throughout the audit.' Timeline: 'Audit plan — Updated whenever new information changes the risk assessment.' The strategy rows carry no such note. AU-C 300.10: the auditor should update and change the overall audit strategy and the audit plan as necessary during the audit.
source: AU-C 300.10; PCAOB AS 2101.15
fix: Reword the takeaway: 'Both the strategy and the plan are updated as necessary throughout the audit; the plan is the more detailed of the two.' Add the same note to the timeline's strategy event.

issue: Correct-choice explanation 'The risk of material misstatement is higher' misstates why: accumulated misstatements approaching materiality raise the risk that undetected plus accumulated misstatements exceed materiality (aggregation/detection side), not the entity's RMM; it also omits asking management to correct.
evidence: AU-C 450.08(b): determine whether the overall strategy and plan need revision when the aggregate of accumulated misstatements approaches materiality; AU-C 450 application guidance (from memory): a greater than acceptably low risk that possible undetected misstatements, with those accumulated, could exceed materiality. Item text: (d) explanation 'Correct. The risk of material misstatement is higher.'
source: AU-C 450.08 and related application guidance
fix: Change to: 'Correct. AU-C 450: when accumulated misstatements approach materiality, the risk that undetected misstatements push the total over materiality is too high, so the auditor revisits the strategy and plan, performs more procedures, and may ask management to correct the misstatements found.'

issue: Thin or off-target choice explanations: they do not state the rule or name the error.
evidence: pl-16 key (a) explanation 'Correct. The strategy sets the overall scope.' explains the strategy, not why NTE is the plan. pl-17 key (b) 'Correct. AU-C 510.' (citation only). pl-20 distractors: (b) 'Compound the changes.', (c) 'Include the rate increase.', (d) 'Include headcount growth.' — instructions, not the error (b = additive 5% + 3% = 8%; c = headcount only; d = rate only).
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 4
fix: pl-16 (a): 'Correct. AU-C 300.09: the plan describes the nature, timing and extent of risk assessment and further audit procedures.' pl-17 (b): 'Correct. AU-C 510.08: obtain sufficient appropriate evidence about whether opening balances contain misstatements that materially affect the current period, and whether policies were applied consistently.' pl-20: '(b) adds 5% + 3% = 8% instead of 1.05 × 1.03; (c) applies only headcount growth; (d) applies only the rate increase.'

issue: Key text 'Setting the engagement's framework, deadlines, and scope' implies the auditor sets the financial reporting framework; the strategy identifies the engagement's characteristics, such as the framework management uses.
evidence: AU-C 300.08(a) / A-guidance: the strategy identifies the characteristics of the engagement that define its scope, such as the financial reporting framework used; the framework is chosen by management.
fix: Reword to 'Identifying the reporting framework, reporting deadlines, and scope of the engagement'.

issue: The lesson omits two AU-C 300 planning requirements a Blueprint II.A task names: planning the nature, timing and extent of direction, supervision and review (AU-C 300.11), and the extra planning activities for an initial audit (AU-C 300.13, e.g., communication with the predecessor).
evidence: grep of lesson: no 'supervis', 'review of their work', 'initial audit' or 'predecessor'. blueprint-tasks.csv AUD-II.A.2 (reconstructed): 'Prepare the engagement strategy and plan, including the nature, timing and extent of direction, supervision and review.' Direction/supervision is mentioned only in aud-quality-management (SAS 146 partner responsibilities).
source: AU-C 300.11, 300.13; AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint Area II.A
fix: Add a short section 'Planning supervision and review; initial audits' (2-3 bullets) and one practice item on each.

issue: The lesson has one pre-question (strategy vs. plan detail) and teaches inventory turnover but not days in inventory or allowance coverage; the module's analysis objective (planning analytics) is not primed, and two ratios used in aud-tbs-u3-analytics are never shown.
evidence: preQuestions: [aud-pl-pre1] only. aud-tbs-u3-analytics asks for days sales in inventory (inventory ÷ (COGS ÷ 365)) and allowance as % of receivables; the lesson's worked example covers gross margin, DSO and turnover only.
source: Lesson design check (review brief §3)
fix: Add a second pre-question on an analytics signal (e.g., 'margin up while industry fell — which accounts would you look at?') and one line in the worked example: 'Days in inventory = 365 ÷ turnover (or inventory ÷ daily COGS)'; mention allowance coverage in the risk step.

issue: Single-rule recall items are labeled skill "analysis" and difficulty 3 (two skill levels too high); dsec-21, -22 and -28 are also flagged calc:true although no computation discriminates among the options.
evidence: dsec-21/-22: every numeric option is $8,000 (only the location differs: OCI vs income vs RE), so the item tests only "AFS -> OCI" / "trading -> NI"; they are near-duplicates (Jaccard 0.83) of each other and of remembering-labeled dsec-11. dsec-23: answer is the label "At amortized cost" (recall that HTM is not marked to FV; same fact as dsec-19, labeled application/2, and far-x2-23, labeled remembering/1). dsec-17 and dsec-25: recall of one ASC 320-10-35-10 transfer rule each, no facts to analyze. dsec-28: recall that CECL applies at purchase; the $4,000 is given in the stem. Blueprint definitions: Remembering & Understanding = knowledge of the topic; Analysis = examining interrelationships to identify causes/find evidence (reconstructed tasks use "analyze, reconcile, detect, investigate and correct"). Batch label counts (practice+exam): application 15, analysis 12, remembering 4 -> after relabeling these six, the module has no analysis-level MCQ that actually requires analysis and remembering rises from 13% to ~32%+ of items, so the section skill-mix target (R&U 5-15, App 45-55, Analysis 35-45) is being met on paper only.
source: AICPA 2026 Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill-level definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel dsec-17, -21, -22, -23, -25, -28 as skill "remembering"; difficulty 1 for -21, -22, -23, -28 and 2 for -17, -25; set calc:false on -21, -22, -28. To keep the analysis share, replace two of them (e.g., -21 and -22) with genuine analysis items (e.g., a two-year AFS roll-forward of amortized cost, FVA balance and AOCI with a sale in year 2, or a classification-reconciliation of a mixed portfolio).

issue: Skill labels one level off: one-step calculations labeled analysis (dsec-05, -16, -18, -24, -26, -27) and pure recall items labeled application (dsec-12, -19, -20, far-x2-13).
evidence: dsec-05/-16/-24: realized gain = proceeds - amortized cost (87,000-80,000; 108,000-100,000; 57,000-50,000) - a one-step "calculate realized gains" (Blueprint reconstructed task FAR-II.E.1.3, Application). dsec-18/-27: allowance = min(ECL, AC-FV) = min(20,000, 15,000) / min(5,000, 3,000) - one-step application. dsec-26: 15,000-6,000 = 9,000 OCI - application. dsec-12: intent to sell -> write down through earnings (no facts to apply). dsec-19: amortized cost 98,000 is given; nothing is computed. dsec-20: which category sends UHG to OCI - recall. far-x2-13: AFS non-credit decline -> $0 in NI (calc:false) - recall.
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprints skill definitions; review/reference/blueprint-tasks.csv FAR-II.E.1.1-E.1.3
fix: Relabel dsec-05, -16, -18, -24, -26, -27 as application; dsec-12, -19, -20 and far-x2-13 as remembering (difficulty 1-2). Recompute the module skill mix after the change.

issue: Distractor trap labels or rationales do not describe the error that produces the number.
evidence: Reproduced each distractor: dsec-16 (c) $6,000 = only the AOCI gain reclassified, but its rationale says "Use amortized cost" (the error is recognizing only the reclassified portion; using amortized cost is what the KEY does). dsec-18 (b) $5,000 = 20,000 ECL - 15,000 shortfall (the unrecognized excess), labeled "reversed" with rationale "That is the excess" - nothing is reversed. dsec-24 (b) $5,000 = AOCI amount only, labeled "wrong-classification" (it is a partial computation; the same error in dsec-05 (b) is labeled partial-computation). dsec-26 (d) "$6,000 in OCI; $9,000 in income" is a swap, labeled "wrong-sign" (identical swap in far-dsec-chk2 (d) is labeled "reversed"). dsec-05 (c) $13,000 = 7,000 + 6,000 double count, labeled "overgeneralization".
source: src/content/schema.ts TRAP_TYPES
fix: dsec-16 (c): "This recognizes only the $6,000 reclassified from AOCI; the realized gain is 108,000 - 100,000 = 8,000." dsec-18 (b): trap partial-computation, "5,000 is the part of the expected loss that the fair-value floor disallows (20,000 - 15,000)." dsec-24 (b): trap partial-computation. dsec-26 (d): trap reversed. dsec-05 (c): trap other (double counting) with rationale "adds the 6,000 AOCI reclassification on top of the 7,000 realized gain".

issue: Thin explanations: item-level explanations state the rule with no computation, and several distractor rationales are circular ("Not the treatment", "Not the computation", "Not for trading", "Not face value").
evidence: Item explanations with no numbers although the item is calc: dsec-13 ("income = carrying amount x effective rate"), -14 (no 200,000-185,000 = 15,000 credit loss vs 30,000 floor; 30,000-15,000 = 15,000 OCI), -15, -16, -18, -24, -26, -27. Circular distractor rationales: dsec-21 (d) "Not the treatment.", -22 (d) "Not the treatment.", -24 (c) "Not the computation.", -25 (d) "Not the treatment.", -27 (d) "Not the computation." (8,000 = 5,000 ECL + 3,000 shortfall), -17 (d) "Not for trading.", -23 (b) "Not face value." Brief section 2 check 4 requires the item explanation to state the rule and show the computation.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 4
fix: Add the computation to each item explanation (e.g., dsec-14: "Credit loss = 200,000 - 185,000 = 15,000, below the 30,000 fair-value floor -> allowance and earnings 15,000; remaining 30,000 - 15,000 = 15,000 to OCI"; dsec-27: "min(5,000 ECL, 100,000 - 97,000 = 3,000) = 3,000"). Rewrite each circular rationale to name the error (e.g., dsec-24 (c): "57,000 is the total proceeds, not the gain"; dsec-25 (d): "transfers never go directly to retained earnings; HTM -> AFS unrealized gains go to OCI under ASC 320-10-35-10(c)").

issue: Stem "unrealized holding gains bypass net income" is literally true of HTM as well (HTM unrealized gains never reach net income), and the explanation for (c) ("Unrealized gains aren't recognized") confirms that they bypass NI; the intended contrast (recognized, but in OCI) is not stated.
evidence: HTM: fair value changes are not recognized (ASC 320-10-35-1(a)); so they also "bypass net income". The key (a) relies on the reader inferring "are recognized outside net income".
fix: Reword: "For which classification of debt securities are unrealized holding gains recognized, but in other comprehensive income rather than net income?"

issue: Answer cue and unanswerable amount: three options are dollar amounts and the key is the only non-numeric label ("At amortized cost"); the stem gives no coupon, yield or term, so the amortized cost cannot be computed, which is why the key avoids a number.
evidence: Options: $99,000 / $100,000 / "At amortized cost" / "$96,000, unchanged". Format mismatch singles out (c). Same fact is tested in dsec-19 and far-x2-23.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 6
fix: Give coupon and yield (e.g., 8% coupon, 9% yield, bought January 1) and key the computed amortized cost ($96,640), with $99,000 (FV), $96,000 (no amortization) and $95,360 (wrong sign) as distractors - or make every option a non-numeric measurement basis. Consider retiring it as redundant with dsec-19.

issue: Weak / implausible distractors.
evidence: dsec-19 (b) $100,000 "Par isn't used" - face value is never given in the stem, so the number has no source; (c) "$4,000 above cost" is not a reportable amount. dsec-24 (c) $57,000 (the total proceeds reported as the gain). far-x2-13 (c) $190,000 (the fair value itself as a loss) and (d) $5,000 (an arbitrary half of the decline). None of these models a misconception a CPA candidate would plausibly hold.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 2
fix: dsec-19: state face $100,000 in the stem and replace (c) with "$98,000 less a $4,000 valuation allowance" or "$100,000 (face)". dsec-24 (c): $2,000 vs $5,000 already cover partial errors; replace with $12,000 (7,000 + 5,000 double count). x2-13 (c)/(d): use "$10,000 in net income as a credit loss" and "$10,000 reclassified to net income at year-end".

issue: Answer cues: the key alone echoes the stem's technical wording.
evidence: chk2 key "$25,000 credit loss in NI; $35,000 in OCI" and dsec-14 key "$15,000 credit loss in earnings; $15,000 in OCI" are the only options that carry the stem term "credit loss" (the parallel reversed option omits it), and both are much the longest (cues.md). dsec-09 stem asks how "expected credit losses" are recognized and only the key says "expected ... credit losses (CECL)"; distractor (b) carries the only absolute ("Only when").
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 6
fix: Make options parallel: e.g., chk2 "(c) $25,000 in net income; $35,000 in OCI" vs "(d) $35,000 in net income; $25,000 in OCI"; dsec-14 drop "credit loss" from the key; dsec-09 change the stem to "How are credit losses on HTM debt securities recognized..." and word the key "Through an allowance measured at lifetime expected losses from initial recognition".

issue: Redundancy: the same three facts are each tested the same way 3-5 times, while multi-step and analysis-level situations are not tested at all.
evidence: Trading UHG -> NI: dsec-04, -11, -22 (+ TBS u7 d4, r3 r4). AFS UHG -> OCI: dsec-20, -21, far-x2-13 (+ pre1, TBS d3, r5). HTM at amortized cost, FV ignored: dsec-19, -23, far-x2-23 (+ TBS d1, r3). AFS sale gain = proceeds - AC with AOCI reclassified: dsec-05, -16, -24 (same template: 80k/87k/6k, 100k/108k/6k, 50k/57k/5k). dsec-21 and -22 are near-identical stems (Jaccard 0.83). Not tested by any MCQ: premium amortization beyond Year 1 / carrying amount after two years, interest income on an AFS security that carries a fair value adjustment, AFS -> HTM transfer, credit-loss recovery (allowance reversal through NI), intent-to-sell write-down with numbers, HTM sale/tainting.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 7
fix: Retire or rewrite dsec-21, -22 (keep -04, -11), dsec-23 (keep -19, x2-23) and one of dsec-16/-24; replace them with items on the untested situations listed, at application/analysis level.

issue: Exam-pool item far-x2-12 reuses practice item dsec-13's bond exactly ($100,000 face, 8% coupon, $96,000 price, 9% yield, HTM), so a candidate who practiced dsec-13 has already computed $8,640 and the mock item measures recall of a seen problem.
evidence: dsec-13 key: 96,000 x 9% = 8,640 interest income. x2-12 key: 96,000 + (8,640 - 8,000) = 96,640 carrying amount - the second step of the same computation on identical numbers.

issue: Lesson-item alignment gap: the lesson never teaches HTM eligibility limits or transfers between categories, yet the inline check far-dsec-chk1 and practice items far-dsec-17 and far-dsec-25 test them (and the item explanations are one-liners), so a learner routed back to the lesson after a miss finds nothing.
evidence: Lesson body: HTM row says only "Positive intent and ability to hold to maturity". Not taught: a security that may be sold in response to interest-rate changes or liquidity needs cannot be HTM (ASC 320-10-25-4) - tested by chk1; the four transfer rules of ASC 320-10-35-10 (from trading: no reversal; into trading: earnings immediately - dsec-17; HTM -> AFS: OCI - dsec-25; AFS -> HTM: AOCI amortized over remaining life, offsetting the premium/discount) and that transfers into or out of trading should be rare (ASC 320-10-35-12). No flashcard covers transfers either.
fix: Add a short "Who qualifies for HTM, and transfers" section after the three-bucket table: the 25-4 disqualifiers, a 4-row transfer table (from/to, measurement at transfer, where the unrealized gain/loss goes), and the "tainting" note for sales/transfers out of HTM; add a flashcard on transfers and cite ASC 320-10-35-10.

issue: Credit-loss measurement is not taught: the lesson says only "the credit portion" goes to an allowance, but never says how the credit loss is measured for AFS (amortized cost minus the present value of expected cash flows at the effective rate, then capped at AC - FV) or that later improvements reverse the allowance through net income. far-dsec-14 depends on the PV-of-expected-cash-flows measure.
evidence: dsec-14: AC 200,000, FV 170,000, PV of expected cash flows 185,000 -> credit loss 200,000 - 185,000 = 15,000 (< 30,000 floor) in earnings, 15,000 OCI. The lesson has no sentence that maps "PV of expected cash flows" to the credit loss; the lesson also has no worked numbers for the cap (tested by dsec-18 and -27).
fix: In "Credit losses", add: "AFS credit loss = amortized cost - PV of expected cash flows (discounted at the effective rate), limited to AC - FV; later decreases in expected losses reverse the allowance through net income." Add a 3-line worked example (e.g., AC 200,000; FV 170,000; PV 185,000 -> 15,000 NI / 15,000 OCI) and one cap example (ECL 20,000 > shortfall 15,000 -> allowance 15,000).

issue: Valuation-account mechanics are not taught: the lesson mentions a "fair value adjustment" account in one sentence but never shows that each period's entry is the change from the existing balance to the required balance, nor the sale/reclassification entry, which far-dsec-08 and the far-tbs-u7-debt-securities journal part require.
evidence: dsec-08: required 158,000 - 150,000 = 8,000 Dr less existing 3,000 Dr -> 5,000 entry. TBS u7 JE: required 390,000 - 385,535 = 4,465 Dr; existing 1,005 Cr -> 5,470 Dr. The lesson's only fair-value example is a first-year adjustment with no prior balance (93,376 -> 95,000 = 1,624).
source: ASC 320-10-35-1; ASC 220-10-45-15 (reclassification adjustments)

issue: Distractor rationales name an error that does not produce the distractor's number (and the trap labels follow the wrong rationale).
evidence: far-eq-08 (d) $(4,000): rationale 'treats the dividend as reducing the investment'. Recomputed: if the 1,000 dividend reduces the investment, carrying amount = 49,000, unrealized loss = 49,000 - 47,000 = 2,000, NI effect = -2,000 (the key), not -4,000. -4,000 = -3,000 unrealized loss - 1,000 (dividend subtracted instead of added), a sign error; trap 'wrong-rule' should be 'wrong-sign'. far-eq-16: (c) $660,000 = 600,000 + 60,000 (omits BOTH the 10,000 amortization and the 15,000 dividends) but its rationale says only 'Dividends reduce the investment' with trap 'wrong-sign' (nothing is sign-reversed: dividends added would give 675,000); (d) $650,000 = 600,000 + 60,000 - 10,000 (omits dividends only) but its rationale says 'Deduct dividends and depreciation'. The (c)/(d) rationales are swapped.
fix: far-eq-08 (d): 'This subtracts the dividend instead of adding it as income (-3,000 - 1,000)'; trap wrong-sign. far-eq-16 (c): 'This omits both the 10,000 excess depreciation and the 15,000 dividend reduction (600,000 + 60,000)'; trap partial-computation. (d): 'This deducts depreciation but omits the 15,000 dividend reduction (600,000 + 60,000 - 10,000)'; trap partial-computation.

issue: Stem omits whether the investor has other investments in or advances to the investee, and the item's own rationale concedes distractor (c) is right in that case.
evidence: Stem: 'reduced to zero by losses. The investor hasn't guaranteed the investee's obligations.' Option (c) 'Recognized against other assets'; its rationale: 'Only if the investor has other investments in the investee.' Under ASC 323-10-35-19 the zero floor applies to 'the investment (and net advances)', and ASC 323-10-35-23 to 35-26 require continued loss recognition against other investments in the investee (preferred stock, loans, advances). The stem is silent, so (c) is conditionally correct. Key (d) 'until income resumes' is also imprecise: the equity method resumes only after the investor's share of later income equals the share of losses not recognized (ASC 323-10-35-22).
fix: Add to the stem: 'and has no other investments in, loans to, or advances to the investee.' Reword (d): 'Not recognized; resumed only after the investor's share of later income equals the unrecognized losses.'

issue: Stem doesn't state the investor is a public business entity, yet distractor (a) 'amortized over 10 years' is true for a private company that elects the goodwill alternative - as the item's own rationale admits.
evidence: (a) rationale: 'Equity-method goodwill is not amortized (except under a private-company election).' Key rationale: 'not amortized (for public entities)'. ASU 2014-02's alternative applies to all goodwill a private company records, including equity-method goodwill, amortized straight-line over 10 years or less. A private-company candidate reading the stem could defend (a).
source: ASU 2014-02 (ASC 350-20-35-62 et seq.; ASC 323-10-35-13); summary at https://www.bakertilly.com/insights/fasb-accounting-standards-offer-gaap-relief-for-private-companies
fix: Stem: 'For a public business entity investor, which of the following is true...' or replace (a) with 'It is amortized over no more than 40 years' (outdated APB 17 rule, trap outdated-rule).

issue: Stem says '$50,000 of the excess of cost over book value relates to equipment' but never says what the rest of the excess relates to (or how large it is).

issue: Answer cues / weak distractors: the key is the only plausible, longest option.

issue: Key 'Cost, adjusted for impairment' omits the observable-price-change adjustment that defines the measurement alternative (and that far-eq-chk1 tests).
evidence: ASC 321-10-35-2: cost minus impairment, plus or minus changes resulting from observable price changes in orderly transactions for the identical or a similar investment of the same issuer. The item explanation includes this, but the keyed text does not, so the key reads as the pre-2018 cost method; a careful candidate may hesitate. far-eq-11 already states it correctly.
fix: Key text: 'Cost less impairment, plus or minus observable price changes for identical or similar securities of the same issuer' (and rebalance option lengths), or retire the item as a duplicate of far-eq-11.

issue: Lesson-item alignment gap: practice items test impairment, partial sale and discontinuance of the equity method, none of which the lesson teaches.
evidence: Lesson body covers classification, FV-NI, measurement alternative, basis differences, intra-entity profit, losses, OCI, becoming equity method and the FVO. It never mentions: other-than-temporary impairment of an equity-method investment and no reversal (far-eq-17; ASC 323-10-35-32); that equity-method goodwill is not separately tested - the whole investment is (far-eq-09; ASC 350-20-35-59); losing significant influence: retained interest keeps its carrying amount as the new basis, then ASC 321 FV-NI (far-eq-18; ASC 323-10-35-36); gain on sale = proceeds - proportionate carrying amount (far-eq-28; ASC 323-10-35-35). Blueprint task FAR-II.E.3.3 (change to or from the equity method) is only half taught. Affected items: far-eq-09, far-eq-17, far-eq-18, far-eq-28 (items themselves are correct).
fix: Add a short 'Impairment, sales and losing influence' subsection: OTT decline -> write down to fair value through earnings, no reversal; equity-method goodwill not tested separately; sale gain = proceeds - (carrying amount x fraction sold); on losing influence the retained carrying amount becomes the basis and the stake is then measured under ASC 321 (FV-NI if readily determinable; observable-transaction remeasurement per ASU 2020-01). Add one inline check on the sale gain.

issue: Basis-difference rule is stated incompletely: the takeaway and flashcard say excess assigned to undervalued assets is 'amortized/depreciated', omitting that an inventory excess is expensed when the inventory is sold and a land excess is not depreciated.
evidence: Key takeaway 4 and far-eq-fc4: 'Assign to undervalued assets (depreciate/amortize through equity income); remainder = goodwill.' TBS far-tbs-u7-equity row inc requires deducting the full 100,000 inventory excess in Year 1 because the inventory was all sold (25% x 1,600,000 = 400,000 - 100,000 - 37,500 = 262,500); a learner following the lesson could try to 'amortize' it. Worked/faded examples use only equipment.
source: ASC 323-10-35-13 (account for basis differences as if the investee were a consolidated subsidiary); ASC 323-10-35-34
fix: Rewrite takeaway 4 / fc4: 'Excess is assigned to specific assets and expensed as those assets are used: depreciable assets over remaining life, inventory when sold (usually Year 1), land not until disposal; remainder = goodwill (not amortized).' Add one worked line with an inventory excess.

issue: Journal part accepts only the single net entry; an equally correct two-entry response (gross share of income, then separate excess amortization) scores 0 of 4.
evidence: Prompt: 'Record Halden's equity in Bryce's earnings for Year 1' (maxLines default 6). Expected lines: Dr Investment in Bryce 117,000 / Cr Equity in earnings of Bryce 117,000. A candidate entering Dr Investment 120,000 / Cr Equity in earnings 120,000 and Dr Equity in earnings 3,000 / Cr Investment 3,000 (a common textbook presentation with identical net effect) gets: both expected cells wrong (amounts 120,000 not 117,000), the two remaining lines are unmatched extra lines charged as wrong cells (src/lib/tbsScoring.ts scoreJournal) -> 0/4 for the part, although the accounting is correct.
source: ASC 323-10-35-4, 35-13; src/lib/tbsScoring.ts
fix: Make the prompt unambiguous: 'Record, in one entry, Halden's equity in Bryce's earnings for Year 1, net of the excess amortization,' and set maxLines to 2 or 4; or support an alternative accepted line set.

issue: Dropdown row d2 relies on vague facts ('ignores the investor') and its explanation is circular.
evidence: d2: '25% of a listed company; a single investor holds the other 75% and ignores the investor' -> keyed FV-NI; explanation: 'Significant influence is lacking despite 25%.' ASC 323-10-15-9 says a majority owner does not by itself preclude significant influence; the presumption is overcome by indicators in ASC 323-10-15-10 (e.g., majority ownership concentrated in a group that operates the investee without regard to the investor's views, failed attempts to obtain board representation or financial information). The row gives no concrete indicator and the explanation teaches none.
fix: Row label: '25% of a listed company; the 75% owner operates the investee without regard to the investor and has refused it a board seat and financial information.' Explanation: 'The 20% presumption is overcome by ASC 323-10-15-10 indicators; with no significant influence the listed shares are measured at FV through net income (ASC 321).'

issue: The 'becoming equity method' and FVO bullets omit two current nuances.
evidence: Lesson: 'add the cost of the new shares to the existing basis and apply the equity method prospectively' and 'The fair value option may be elected ... (irrevocably, at initial recognition).' (1) ASU 2020-01 (ASC 321-10-35-1A): an investor using the measurement alternative must remeasure the previously held interest for an observable transaction (such as the purchase that triggers significant influence) immediately before applying the equity method. (2) ASC 825-10-25-4 also permits the FVO election on the date an investment first becomes subject to the equity method, not only at initial recognition.
fix: Add: 'If the old stake used the measurement alternative, first remeasure it for the observable transaction (ASU 2020-01).' Change FVO wording to 'irrevocably, at initial recognition or when the investment first becomes subject to the equity method.'

issue: The only pre-question primes FV-NI for passive stakes; nothing primes the equity method, which is the lesson's main (analysis-labeled) objective.
evidence: preQuestions: [far-eq-pre1] (5% public stock gain -> net income). The equity method mechanics (income share up, dividends down, basis-difference amortization) take most of the body and both worked/faded blocks but have no pre-question; far-eq-chk2 is the first touchpoint.

issue: Pure recall item (a declared cash dividend payable in 30 days is a current liability) is labeled skill 'analysis', difficulty 3 — two levels off on both; it inflates the module's analysis share.
evidence: Stem asks only how a declared cash dividend is reported at year-end; no computation, no data to analyze, calc unset.
