The 11 'analysis' labels in this module's practice+exam pool (cues.md) give 37% analysis; this item is one of them.
source: AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint skill definitions
fix: Set skill: remembering, difficulty: 1. Optionally replace with an analysis-level item (e.g., detect a misclassified dividend in a draft current-liabilities schedule).

issue: Three practice items test rules taught nowhere on the platform: supplier finance program disclosures (ASU 2022-04 / ASC 405-50) and gift-card breakage recognized in proportion to redemptions (ASC 606-10-55-48). The payables lesson's objectives, body and takeaways never mention either, and no other FAR lesson does.
evidence: grep -rli 'breakage' content/far -> only far-payables/questions.json; grep -rli 'supplier finance' content/far -> only far-payables/questions.json. far-pay-19 (10,000 x 45/90 = 5,000 breakage; revenue 50,000) and far-pay-25 (5,000 x 30/45 = 3,333; liability 16,667) require the proportional method; far-pay-18 requires the ASC 405-50-50-3 disclosure list (key terms, confirmed amount outstanding, balance sheet location, rollforward). Supplier finance obligations are a payables-specific FAR II.G topic, testable since FY > 12/15/2022 (rollforward FY > 12/15/2023).
source: ASC 405-50-50-3; ASC 606-10-55-46 to 55-49; review/reference/far-standards.md (ASU 2022-04)
fix: Add a short lesson section 'Other current liabilities': supplier finance programs (what the buyer discloses, AP vs. separate presentation), contract liabilities for gift cards with the proportional breakage method (worked example) and the remote-likelihood alternative when no breakage is expected, plus a matching flashcard each.

issue: Numeric distractor rationales do not name the error that produces the number: several say only 'Not the computation.' (trap 'distractor-number') although the number models a real misconception, and far-pay-03(d) names the wrong error.
evidence: Reproduced: 03(d) 50,300 = 32,000 withheld + 15,300 employer FICA + 3,000 unemployment (correct expense + income-tax withholding); the rationale says it 'includes income tax withheld and employee FICA', which would be 18,300+32,000+15,300 = 65,600. 25(c) 15,000 = 50,000-30,000-5,000 (all breakage recognized up front); 25(d) 18,000 = (50,000-30,000) x 90% (breakage applied to the unredeemed balance) — both 'Not the computation.' 26(c) 19,800 = 10% x (220,000-22,000) (deducting a first-pass bonus) — 'Not the computation.'; 26(d) 18,000 has no derivation from the stem. 27(b) 19,800 = 1% discount; 27(d) 18,000 = reading '2/10' as 10% — both 'Not the computation.' 24(b) 5,640 = 6,000-360 and x2-05(d) 28,200 = 30,000-1,800 are mirror numbers with no misconception ('no such calculation applies').
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 2
fix: Rewrite each rationale to state the error: 03(d) 'adds the employees' income-tax withholding to the employer's expense'; 25(c) 'recognizes all expected breakage immediately'; 25(d) 'applies 10% to the unredeemed balance instead of the proportional method'; 26(c) 'deducts a bonus computed on the full 220,000'; 27(b) 'uses 1%'; 27(d) 'reads 2/10 as a 10% discount'. Replace the three distractors that model no error: 24(b) -> $100,000 (the sales amount, trap reversed); x2-05(d) -> $500,000 (the corrected sales, reversed); 26(d) -> $24,444 = 22,000 / 0.9 (adds the bonus to the base instead of deducting it, wrong-sign). Set trap labels to match.

issue: Implausible distractors make the key obvious and the rationales are thin: far-pay-18 offers 'Nothing beyond accounts payable' and 'Only the bank's name'; far-pay-20 offers 'reduction of inventory' and 'equity' with rationales 'Not the treatment.' and 'They're owed back.'
evidence: 18: only (a) and (c) are plausible; (d) also carries the absolute 'Only' and (b) 'Nothing' (cue: absolutes in distractors only). 18(c) rationale 'The buyer's program terms.' does not explain why the financing rate is not required. 20(b) rationale 'Not the treatment.' is circular.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ checks 2, 4, 6
fix: 18: use distractors from real confusions — e.g., 'Only the amount outstanding; no rollforward', 'The supplier's discount rate and the bank's fee', 'Reclassify the confirmed amount to short-term debt'. 20: use 'Revenue when collected, with an allowance for expected refunds', 'A contingent liability, disclosed only', and explain each.

issue: Trap labels that do not match the misconception the option models.
evidence: chk1(b) $20,000 = the 2 unworked days (Thu-Fri) is labeled partial-computation, while the identical option in far-pay-21(c) is labeled 'reversed' (the correct label). 18(d) 'Only the bank's name' is labeled partial-computation on a non-numeric disclosure item (should be wrong-rule). 19(d) $100,000 (all revenue at sale) is labeled overgeneralization; the error is timing (wrong-period). 28(b) 'noncurrent liability' is labeled wrong-rule; it is a classification error (wrong-classification).
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 2
fix: Relabel: chk1(b) reversed; 18(d) wrong-rule; 19(d) wrong-period; 28(b) wrong-classification.

issue: Skill (and difficulty) labels off by one level. far-pay-19 and -21 to -27 are single-formula calculations labeled 'analysis', difficulty 3; far-pay-18 and -20 are pure recall labeled 'application'. The pattern inflates the module's analysis share (11 of 30 = 37%, inside the 35-45% target only because of these labels).
evidence: 21: 3/5 x 50,000 = 30,000 (difficulty 3 vs the identical lesson check chk1 labeled application). 22: 7,650 + 2,000 (identical to far-pay-17, labeled application/2). 23: 20x10x200x60% = 24,000. 24: 106,000 - 106,000/1.06 = 6,000 (same as far-pay-02, application/2). 26: B = 22,000/1.1 = 20,000 (same as the lesson's faded example). 27: 20,000 x 98% = 19,600. 19/25: one proportional breakage step; the FAR Blueprint keeps revenue recognition at Remembering/Application only — analysis-level revenue tasks moved to BAR (blueprint-notes.md l.130). 18: recall of an ASC 405-50 disclosure list; 20: recall that refundable deposits are liabilities. With these relabeled, the module's MCQ analysis share falls to ~2 of 30 (05, 11).
source: AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint skill definitions; review/reference/blueprint-notes.md
fix: Relabel 19, 21-27 as application with difficulty 1-2 (21, 27: 1; 22, 23, 24, 26: 2; 19, 25: 2-3); relabel 18 and 20 as remembering. If the module needs analysis-level MCQs, write genuine ones (e.g., identify which accrual in a schedule is misstated and by how much).

issue: Verbatim-duplicate pairs: far-pay-21 repeats lesson check chk1 (same $50,000 weekly payroll, 5-day week paid Friday, Wednesday year-end, key $30,000); far-pay-22 repeats far-pay-17 (same $100,000 wages, 7.65% employer FICA, $2,000 unemployment, key $9,650).
evidence: Same facts, same numbers, same key in each pair; cues.md flags 17~22 (Jaccard 0.50). A learner who did the lesson check meets the same question in practice and answers from memory. Employer payroll tax expense is also tested by far-pay-03, so 3 practice items test it the same way.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7
fix: Rewrite far-pay-21 with different facts (e.g., Thursday year-end with a holiday, or a biweekly payroll) and far-pay-22 as a variant that adds value (e.g., one employee above the Social Security wage base, or FUTA limited to the first $7,000 per employee, with the bases given).

issue: Redundancy: backing sales tax out of tax-inclusive receipts is tested the same way four times (plus the lesson's worked example and flashcard fc2), each with the same 'X% x total' distractor.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7 (>3 times)
fix: Keep pre1 and x2-05; replace far-pay-24 (or 02) with a different sales-tax angle — e.g., the journal entry to reclassify, sales tax on a mix of taxable and exempt sales, or the remittance entry.

issue: Lesson-item alignment gaps: items test liabilities the lesson never covers — contract liabilities for gift cards (14) and subscriptions (16), refundable bottle and customer deposits (20, 09c), dividends payable and stock dividend distributable (09, 28) — and the after-tax bonus formula (05; the lesson and fc5 show only 'after bonus, before tax').
evidence: Lesson body sections: AP gross/net, accrued expenses, sales tax/payroll, compensated absences, bonus (before-tax only), AP reconciliation, ASC 420. No mention of unearned revenue, deposits, gift cards or dividends. 'Stock dividend distributable' appears in no FAR lesson (grep). Contract liabilities are taught in far-revenue-measurement and dividends in far-equity, both sequenced after far-payables. far-pay-05 needs B = 0.20 x 0.75 x (345,000 - B) -> 45,000, a two-equation setup the lesson never demonstrates.
source: Review brief §3 lesson-item alignment and sequencing
fix: Add an 'Other current liabilities' section (unearned revenue/contract liabilities, refundable deposits, dividends payable vs. stock dividend distributable in equity) and a second bonus example with taxes (B = r x (I - B - T), T = t x (I - B)); add a flashcard for the after-tax bonus.

issue: Stem omits the beginning warranty liability (or that 2025 is the first year of sales); the liability cannot be computed without it, and the lesson stresses the roll-forward 'beginning liability + expense - claims paid'.
evidence: Key 12,000 = 0 + 2% x 1,000,000 - 8,000 assumes a zero beginning balance that the stem never states. The companion TBS (far-tbs-u8-accruals-review) gives a $11,000 beginning balance, so learners are trained to look for one.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 3
fix: Add 'its first year of selling the product' or 'The warranty liability at January 1, 2025 was $0.'

issue: The lesson's AP reconciliation table says a payment posted to the wrong vendor needs correcting in 'Neither total (but two vendor balances)', while the AP-recon TBS asks which record must be corrected and keys 'Subledger only' with 'Neither record' as an option. A learner following the lesson's wording is steered to the option the TBS scores wrong.
evidence: Lesson table column 'Correct': 'Payment posted to the wrong vendor | Neither total (but two vendor balances)'. TBS part src row d4 answer 'Subledger only' — explanation: 'The subledger total is unaffected, but two vendor balances are wrong.' The TBS key is right (the vendor accounts in the subledger must be corrected).
source: Internal consistency (review brief §2 consistency)
fix: Change the lesson row to 'Subledger only — move it between the two vendor accounts; neither total changes.'

issue: Item-level explanations state the rule but not the computation (and some correct-choice explanations are bare), contrary to the 'explanations teach' standard.
evidence: 21: 'Accrued wages are earned but unpaid at year-end.' (no 50,000/5 = 10,000 x 3). 25: no final 50,000 - 30,000 - 3,333 = 16,667. 26: 'Solve algebraically...' (no 1.1B = 22,000 -> 20,000). 27: 'discounts taken are recorded at payment' (no 20,000 x 2% = 400; cash 19,600). 17/22: rule only (7,650 + 2,000 appears only in choice text). 23: rule only. 26(a) 'The bonus is after itself.' is unclear.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 4
fix: Add the worked computation to each item-level explanation, e.g. 26: 'B = 0.10 x (220,000 - B) -> 1.10B = 22,000 -> B = 20,000; check 10% x 200,000 = 20,000.' Rewrite 26(a): 'Takes 10% of income before deducting the bonus.'

issue: far-pay-03 and far-pay-17 do not say wages are below the Social Security and FUTA wage bases (far-pay-22 does), and the lesson's payroll section gives FICA at 7.65% without mentioning the per-employee wage bases.
evidence: 03: gross payroll $200,000 with FICA 7.65% 'for both' — key 15,300 assumes no employee exceeds the 2026 Social Security wage base ($184,500, from memory). Exam stems usually state the assumption.
source: IRC §3111, §3121(a)(1); SSA 2026 wage base (from memory)
fix: Add 'All wages are below the FICA and unemployment wage bases' to 03 and 17; add one sentence to the lesson that the 6.2% Social Security portion and FUTA apply only up to per-employee wage bases (given on the exam), and that Medicare 1.45% has no cap.

issue: Goods received but not invoiced are keyed as an addition to the vendor open-invoice subledger (grni +12,400; d3 'Both records'). Many entities record such receipts only as a general-ledger accrual (received-not-invoiced), so 'General ledger only' is a defensible reading.
evidence: Exhibit calls the subledger an 'open-invoice subledger' and says no invoice has arrived; an open-invoice subledger normally holds only invoices. The reconciliation's 'subledger side' row cues the intended answer, so scoring is consistent, but the premise is unstated.
source: ASC 405-10 (recognition); common AP practice
fix: Add to the exhibit: 'Brightwater records received-not-invoiced goods in the vendor's subledger account at purchase-order price', or change the d3 explanation to acknowledge the alternative.

issue: Wording: the iexp explanation says interest expense 'is always twelve months ... whatever the payment dates' (true only for a note outstanding all year), and the payroll exhibit says 'paid in arrears' although each payday covers work through that day.
evidence: Recomputed keys are correct: wages 84,000/10 x 5 = 42,000; interest 600,000 x 6% x 3/12 = 9,000; warranty 11,000 + 48,000 - 29,500 = 29,500; total 105,000; warranty expense 48,000; interest expense 36,000. Only the wording overgeneralizes.
fix: iexp: 'Because the note was outstanding all year, interest expense is twelve months...'. Exhibit: drop 'paid in arrears' or say 'paid on the last day of each period'.

issue: The lesson has a single pre-question (far-pay-pre1, sales tax) that primes a minor topic, not the big idea (accrue what has been incurred but not paid) or the reconciliation/completeness concept the analysis objective targets.
evidence: frontmatter preQuestions: [far-pay-pre1]; the big idea and four of five objectives concern accruals, payroll, bonus, reconciliation and ASC 420.
source: Review brief §3 lesson design
fix: Add a pre-question on accrual timing (e.g., December utility bill received in January) or on what an agreeing AP reconciliation does and does not prove.

issue: The ASC 420 section omits the cease-use-date rule for costs that continue under a contract without economic benefit, and the citations list omits ASC 420, ASC 712, ASC 405-50 and ASC 835-30 although the body and items rely on them.
evidence: Lesson table rows: termination benefits (2), contract termination, other costs; ASC 420-10-25-13 (costs continuing without economic benefit recognized at the cease-use date) not shown — far-pay-13(d) 'over the remaining contract term' touches it. Frontmatter citations: 405-10, 710-10-25, 606-10-32-2A only.
fix: Add a row 'Costs that continue under a contract with no economic benefit — at the cease-use date'; add citations ASC 420-10-25, ASC 712-10-25, ASC 405-50-50 and ASC 835-30-15-3.

issue: 'What liability is accrued?' — accrual of nonvesting accumulating sick pay is not required but is not prohibited, so $110,000 is a permissible policy; the stem should ask for the required amount.
evidence: ASC 710-10-25-7 says an employer is not required to accrue nonvesting accumulating sick pay; the key $80,000 is the minimum required.
fix: Reword to 'What liability must be accrued?' (as far-pay-15 does).

issue: Discipline picker shows placeholder labels "BAR — BAR" and "ISC — ISC" because those sections have no content; the learner cannot tell what BAR/ISC are or that they have no material.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j1-d-02-sections.png. Steps: fresh context -> #/welcome -> "Got it" -> open "Which discipline section will you take?" -> options read "BAR — BAR", "ISC — ISC", "TCP — Tax Compliance and Planning". Code: Onboarding.tsx falls back to `?? d` when content.sections lacks the id.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Add a static name map (BAR = Business Analysis and Reporting, ISC = Information Systems and Controls) and suffix "(no content yet)" for sections not in content.sections.
expected: Full section names, with a note when a section has no content.
steps: Open #/welcome in a fresh context, click "Got it — set up my plan", open the discipline select.

issue: The lesson completion button promises "Mark complete & practice (28 questions)" but opens a 10-question set. The count is every practice item in the module (questionsForModule), while PracticeStart builds the set with count: 10.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j2-d-09-before-complete.png (button label "Mark complete & practice (28 questions)"), review/screens/uj-j2-d-10-after-complete.png (quiz header "0/10 answered"). Steps: onboard FAR -> #/module/far-income-statement-oci -> scroll to "Finished reading?" -> click the button.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Label the button with the set size actually served, e.g. "Mark complete & practice (10 questions)" (Math.min(10, practiceCount)), or "practice 10 of 28 questions".
expected: The button states the number of questions in the set it starts.
steps: Open a lesson, click "Mark complete & practice (N questions)", compare N with the quiz header.

issue: Inline lesson questions each show a "Highlight selection" tool, but every McqView writes to one global CSS highlight ("exam-highlight"), so highlighting text in the second check question silently erases the highlight in the first. These question highlights are also ephemeral, while the lesson's own "Save highlight" is persistent: two unrelated highlight behaviours on one page.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j2b-d-03-check1-highlight-after-check2.png. Steps (desktop): open #/module/far-income-statement-oci, select the first words of check 1's stem, click its "Highlight selection" (CSS.highlights.get("exam-highlight").size = 1), do the same in check 2 -> size is still 1 and check 1's highlight is gone.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Hide the ephemeral highlight tool on inline lesson questions (showTools=false should cover it), or key the CSS highlight name per question (e.g. `exam-highlight-${q.id}` registered in CSS) so instances do not overwrite each other.
expected: Highlights in one inline question survive highlighting another, or the tool is not offered in lessons.
observed: Only the latest question keeps its highlight.
steps: Highlight text in two different "Check your understanding" questions on one lesson.

issue: Saved lesson highlights appear only in a list at the bottom of the page; the highlighted passage is not marked in the lesson text, and text in the warm-up question, "big idea" box and key takeaways cannot be highlighted (selection there shows no "Save highlight" button) although the tip says "select any text in the lesson".
evidence: review/screens/uj-j2b-d-01-body-selection.png, review/screens/uj-j2b-d-02-highlight-list.png, review/screens/uj-j2-d-07-selection.png. Steps: select a sentence in the body -> "Save highlight" -> no <mark>/CSS highlight in the body (count 0); select text in the pre-question explanation -> no button.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Render saved highlights inline (CSS Custom Highlight API or <mark>) and widen bodyRef to the big idea and takeaways, or reword the tip to "select text in the lesson body".

issue: The results page miscounts what entered spaced review. It reports missed + guessed-right, but needsRequeue() also queues correct answers rated "Unsure"; and when nothing was missed it says "Clean sweep. These will stay out of your review queue." even when Unsure answers were queued, or when half the test-mode set was unanswered and scored wrong (50%).
evidence: Tutor set: 1 wrong-Unsure, 1 wrong-Confident, 1 right-Guess, 1 right-Unsure -> IndexedDB srs table has 4 q: rows, page says "3 question(s) were added" (review/screens/uj-j3-d-06-results.png). Test set with 2 answered correctly and 2 unanswered -> "50% ... 2 questions were left unanswered and scored as wrong. Clean sweep." (review/screens/uj-j3-d-12-test-results.png).
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Compute the count from the same rule as scheduling (answered && needsRequeue(correct, confidence ?? "confident")), and show "Clean sweep" only when every item was answered correctly with confidence; otherwise say e.g. "No questions were added to review; 2 unanswered questions were scored wrong."
expected: The count matches the questions actually queued; "Clean sweep" only for a perfect set.
observed: Undercounts by the Unsure-correct items; "Clean sweep" at 50%.
steps: Practice a module in tutor mode answering one item correctly with "Unsure"; then run a 4-question test-mode set leaving 2 unanswered.

issue: In test mode an answer chosen without a confidence rating is scored, and the question navigator marks it answered, but the header and Submit button count it as unanswered ("0/4 answered"). Submitting with unanswered questions gives no warning or confirmation.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j3-m-11-test-last.png, review/screens/uj-j3-d-11-test-last.png. Steps: #/practice -> tick Area I -> 4 questions -> Test -> Timed -> Start; pick a choice on Q1 only -> header shows "0/4 answered" while the navigator square 1 is filled; Q1 is later scored Correct. On Q4 "Submit set (1/4)" submits at once.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Count answeredCount by `choice` alone in test mode (confidence is optional there), and when unanswered items remain show a confirm step ("2 questions unanswered will be scored wrong. Submit anyway?") listing them.
expected: One definition of "answered" across header, navigator and scoring; a confirmation before submitting with blanks.
observed: Header says 0 answered while the navigator and scoring treat the item as answered; no confirmation.
steps: Run a test-mode custom set as above.

issue: Keyboard shortcut race: pressing a choice letter and then a confidence digit in quick succession (under ~50 ms, e.g. a fast typist or a key macro) drops the confidence key silently, because the hotkey handler checks the rendered `selected` prop, which updates only after the IndexedDB write round-trips.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j3c-d-keyboard-race.png. Steps (desktop): #/practice/start?module=far-bonds -> press "d" then "2" back-to-back -> D is selected (aria-checked=true) but no feedback appears; pressing "2" again submits. With a 150 ms gap it works first time.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Track the last chosen letter in a ref inside McqView (set on onSelect) and let the confidence key use it when `selected` has not caught up yet.

issue: A flashcard session has no way to stop early: there is no End/Exit button, Escape does nothing, and the "Flashcard decks" navigation entry (same route) keeps the learner inside the session because the session lives in component state. The only exit is to navigate to a different page.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j4-d-07-nav-decks-still-in-session.png, review/screens/uj-j4-m-07-nav-decks-still-in-session.png. Steps: complete a lesson -> #/flashcards?module=far-income-statement-oci -> "Study this deck" -> click "Flashcard decks" in the sidebar (desktop) or More > Flashcard decks (phone) -> still on the card ("8 left in this session"); press Escape -> still in session.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Add an "End session" button beside "N left in this session" that calls onDone (graded cards are already saved), and reset `session` when the location key changes (or put the session in the URL, e.g. ?study=1) so the nav entry returns to the deck list.
expected: A visible way to end a session; the "Flashcard decks" link shows the deck list.
observed: No exit control; the nav link leaves the learner on the card.
steps: Start any flashcard session and try to get back to the deck list.

issue: Cards graded Again/Hard/Good on a new card are rescheduled minutes later (1m / 6m / 10m), but if the learner reloads or leaves, those cards are not in the resumed session and the review page says "0 due" until the minutes pass; the done screen never says they will return later today.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j4-d-03-card-back.png (grade labels "Again 1m, Hard 6m, Good 10m, Easy 8d"), review/screens/uj-j4-d-04-after-reload.png ("0 due · 4 new today" after grading 4 of 8). Steps: study 8 new cards, grade the first four Again/Hard/Good/Easy, reload.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: On the done screen and the review page, show "N cards come back in a few minutes" (count of srs cards due later today), and offer a short "Study again" when they become due.

issue: Rows labelled only "1"…"7" (the situations live in an exhibit tab). On a phone there is no split view, so the learner must switch between the "Situations" tab and the "Task" tab for every row, and the results list shows "✗ 1 — You: Not a violation · Answer: Violation" without restating the situation. Same pattern in far-tbs-r3-property-tax, aud-tbs-r3-journal-entries and aud-tbs-r3-it-coso.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j5-m-aud-tbs-r3-conduct-rules-b-partial-full.png (phone: seven selects labelled 1–7, results "✗ 1"). Steps: phone viewport -> #/tbs/aud-tbs-r3-conduct-rules -> answer the 7 rows (each needs a trip to the "Situations" tab) -> submit with row 1 wrong.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Give each row a short descriptive label (e.g. "1. Contingent fee — original return"), or on narrow screens render the matching exhibit paragraph under each row label; in TbsResults show the row label text plus the situation excerpt.
expected: Each row and each result cell identifies the situation it scores.
observed: Bare numbers; the phone layout forces tab switching per row.
steps: Open the TBS on a 390px viewport.

issue: Submitting a simulation scrolls to the very bottom of the page, past the "Score: x/y cells" heading, so on both viewports the learner first sees the last cell and the action buttons, not the score. "Submit" with blank cells and "Try again from scratch" (which deletes the saved run) both act without confirmation.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j5-d-far-tbs-u1-income-statement-b-partial-score.png (viewport after submit: last cells and buttons, no score heading). Code: TbsPage.submit() -> window.scrollTo({ top: document.body.scrollHeight }).
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Scroll the #tbs-results heading into view and focus it; confirm "Submit with N blank cells?" and "Discard this attempt and start over?".

issue: Submitting a testlet asks only "Submit testlet N? You will not be able to return to it." It does not say how many questions are unanswered or which are flagged for review, so the flag-for-review tool never pays off at the one moment it matters (the real exam shows a review summary before a testlet is submitted).
evidence: review/screens/uj-j6-d-07-submit-confirm.png (testlet 1 with Q3 flagged: confirm text has no mention of it). Testlet 2 submitted with 5 of 25 unanswered: same text, no warning. Steps: #/exam -> Start FAR Simulated Exam 1 -> flag Q3 -> answer 20 of 25 in testlet 2 -> "Submit testlet".
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: In the confirm card list "Unanswered: 21, 22, 23, 24, 25" and "Flagged: 3" as buttons that jump to the item, and make the primary action read "Submit with 5 unanswered" when any are blank.
expected: A pre-submit summary of unanswered and flagged items.
steps: Flag an item, leave some blank, press "Submit testlet".

issue: The calculator and spreadsheet open as fixed panels that cannot be moved. On a phone the calculator (256×344 px at y 404–748 of 844) covers the lower stem and choices A–B, and the spreadsheet covers most of the screen. The calculator also ignores Backspace and loses its display and memory each time it is closed and reopened.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j6-m-02-calculator-overlay.png, review/screens/uj-j6-m-03-spreadsheet-overlay.png, review/screens/uj-j6-d-04-calculator.png. Steps: phone viewport -> start a mock -> tap the calculator icon. Desktop: 100 / 3 = 33.3333333333, Backspace -> unchanged; close and reopen -> display "0", memory cleared.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Make the panels draggable (or dock them as a collapsible bottom sheet on narrow screens that pushes content up), handle Backspace to delete the last digit, and keep calculator state in the parent (ExamRunner/QuizPlayer) so closing only hides it.
expected: Tools that can be moved off the item and keep their state while the item is open.
observed: Fixed overlays covering the question; state reset on close; no Backspace.
steps: Open the calculator on a 390px viewport during a mock exam.

issue: On the last testlet the button says "Submit exam", but the confirmation still reads "Submit testlet 5? You will not be able to return to it." with a "Submit testlet" button, so it is not clear that this ends the exam and shows the score.
evidence: review/screens/uj-j6-d-11-final-confirm.png. Steps: reach testlet 5 of FAR Simulated Exam 1 -> "Submit exam".

Focus on spaced review, mixed practice and your weakest areas", yet the schedule puts a 4-hour mock exam today (before any lesson) and fills tomorrow with about 15 new lessons and practice sets (learning work "spills into final review if behind"). issue: Updates are only discovered when the page loads: useRegisterSW({ immediate: true }) sets up no periodic registration.update(), and the app is a HashRouter SPA, so an installed PWA or a tab left open for days never learns about a new deploy until it is relaunched. "Later" hides the toast until the next full load (it does reappear after a reload, and Reload is correctly withheld during quizzes, simulations and mocks).
evidence: Code reading of UpdatePrompt.tsx; in the walkthrough the toast appeared only after an explicit registration.update() (logs/j8u-run.txt). Behaviour verified: busy routes show no Reload; after leaving the quiz Reload appears; after "Later" + in-app navigation no toast; after a plain reload it returns; Reload activates the new worker and an in-progress mock stays resumable.
source: Hands-on walkthrough (Playwright, Chromium) of the built app on vite preview :4173
fix: Pass onRegisteredSW(url, r) { setInterval(() => r?.update(), 60 * 60 * 1000) } and also call r.update() on visibilitychange to visible.

issue: Distractor (b) explanation teaches a wrong rule: it says 'Disclosure is for remote cases.' Under ASC 470-10-45-2, when acceleration under a subjective acceleration clause is remote, neither reclassification nor disclosure is required; disclosure alone applies to the middle case (acceleration reasonably possible). The item-level explanation also gives only the 'probable' tier.
evidence: Choice (b) explanation: 'Disclosure is for remote cases.' ASC 470-10-45-2: some circumstances (recurring losses, liquidity problems) call for current classification; others call only for disclosure of the clause; 'Neither reclassification nor disclosure would be required if the likelihood of the acceleration of the due date were remote.' Key (d) Current is right.
fix: Rewrite (b) explanation: 'Disclosure alone applies when acceleration is reasonably possible but not probable; if it is remote, neither reclassification nor disclosure is needed. Here acceleration is probable, so the debt is current.' Expand the item explanation to state all three tiers (probable: current; reasonably possible: disclose; remote: nothing).

issue: Six practice items (21% of the module's 28) test topics that this lesson never teaches, and no other FAR lesson teaches them either: debt with detachable warrants (dbt-14), convertible debt at issuance and on conversion after ASU 2020-06 (dbt-15, dbt-19), derecognition only on payment or legal release / in-substance defeasance (dbt-26), line-of-credit issuance costs (dbt-27) and subjective acceleration clauses (dbt-28). A learner who misses them is routed to a lesson with nothing to read.
evidence: Lesson headings: Notes payable at present value; Current or noncurrent?; Extinguishment; Disclosures; Debt covenant compliance; Modification, extinguishment and TDRs. grep -i 'detachable|convertible|defeas|subjective|line.of.credit|revolv' over content/far/modules/*/lesson.md finds only EPS if-converted text (far-eps) and 'readily convertible' (far-cash, far-ratios). far-bonds lesson (prerequisite) covers pricing, effective interest, issuance costs and between-dates issuance only, although far-bond-15/-26/-27 also test convertibles and warrants.
fix: Add a short section 'Other debt topics' (here, or in far-bonds with dbt-14/15/19 moved there) teaching: (1) bonds with detachable warrants: allocate by relative fair values when both are known, incremental method when only one is; (2) convertible debt after ASU 2020-06: all proceeds to debt unless a derivative or substantial premium; conversion per original terms moves the carrying amount to equity with no gain or loss; (3) debt is derecognized only when paid or legally released, so in-substance defeasance leaves the debt on the books; (4) line-of-credit costs may be deferred as an asset and amortized ratably; (5) subjective acceleration clauses: probable acceleration means current, reasonably possible means disclose, remote means nothing. Add one inline check and a flashcard.

issue: Pure-recall items are labeled skill 'analysis' with difficulty 3, which is two levels off. Each asks for a single rule stated directly by the facts (in-substance defeasance keeps the debt on the books; revolver costs may be an asset; probable acceleration means current), with no computation and no interrelationships to examine. This inflates the module's analysis share, which feeds the Blueprint skill-mix targets.
evidence: dbt-26: 'places risk-free securities in an irrevocable trust... isn't legally released. What is the accounting?' dbt-27: 'costs to obtain a revolving line of credit with nothing drawn. How are the costs presented?' dbt-28: 'subjective acceleration clause, and acceleration is probable. How is it classified?' Compare dbt-05 and dbt-15 (same kind of recall), which are labeled remembering, difficulty 1.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions (Remembering and Understanding vs Analysis); content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel dbt-26, dbt-27 and dbt-28 as skill 'remembering', difficulty 1 (dbt-28 could be 2 once the three-tier rule is taught).

issue: Application-level items are labeled 'analysis' (mostly difficulty 3), one level off. Each applies one stated rule or one or two arithmetic steps. The clearest case: dbt-23 and dbt-24 are the same computations as dbt-01 and dbt-02 (PV of a 2-year noninterest-bearing note, then Year-1 effective interest), yet they are labeled analysis/3 while dbt-01 and dbt-02 are application/2.
evidence: dbt-23: 100,000/1.10^2 = 82,645 (analysis, 3) vs dbt-01: 200,000/1.08^2 = 171,468 (application, 2). dbt-24: 82,645 x 10% (analysis, 3) vs dbt-02: 171,468 x 8% (application, 2). dbt-21: 110,000 - 90,000 = 20,000 gain. dbt-22 and dbt-16: two subtractions. dbt-18 and dbt-25: apply the grace-period / more-than-one-year waiver rule. dbt-03: apply ASC 470-10-45-15. If relabeled, the module's practice mix is about 5 remembering / 22 application / 1 analysis (dbt-10), against 12 analysis as labeled.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation (analysis 35-45%)
fix: Relabel dbt-03, 16, 18, 21, 22, 23, 24 and 25 as 'application'. Set difficulty 2 for 23/24 (to match 01/02) and 18/21/25. Then add genuine analysis-level items or a TBS (see the pedagogy finding).

issue: Distractor (a) '$40,000 loss' is explained as 'This ignores the premium', but ignoring the premium gives a $40,000 GAIN, which is choice (c), and (c)'s rationale ('compares the price with face only') describes that same error. The rationale for (a) names an error that does not produce (a)'s number. Its partial-computation trap label is wrong too.
evidence: Ignore premium: 2,000,000 - 1,960,000 = +40,000 gain (choice c). A $40,000 loss needs that error plus a sign reversal (or reading 98 as 102: 2,040,000 - 2,040,000 = 0, so that is not it either). Key: 2,040,000 - 1,960,000 = 80,000 gain (d), confirmed.
fix: Either relabel (a) as 'Ignores the premium and reverses the sign (treats paying below face as a loss)' with trap wrong-sign, or replace (a) with 'No gain or loss' (subtracts the $40,000 premium as if it were a discount: 1,960,000 - 1,960,000 = 0; trap wrong-sign).

issue: For three distractors, the stem cannot produce the number, or the rationale doesn't name the error that does. dbt-13 (b) $220,000 needs a discount rate (about 10%) that the stem never gives. dbt-21 (d) $10,000 cannot be derived from 110,000 and 90,000, and is explained only as 'Not the computation.' dbt-23 (d) $80,000 is the simple-interest discount (100,000 - 2 x 10% x 100,000), but its rationale just says 'Not the computation.'
evidence: dbt-13: 550,000 - 400,000/1.10^2 = 219,421, about 220,000, but only at an unstated 10%; no rate appears in the stem. dbt-21: no pairing of 110,000 and 90,000 gives 10,000 (110-90 = 20; 90/9 = 10 is not meaningful). dbt-23: 100,000 x (1 - 0.10 x 2) = 80,000.
fix: dbt-13: add 'The market rate is 10%' to the stem as a red herring, and say in (b) 'PV at 10% = 330,579; gain 219,421, about 220,000; the debtor test uses undiscounted payments.' dbt-21: replace (d) with a modeled error, e.g. 'A $20,000 gain deferred and recognized over the new term' (wrong-period) or '$90,000 gain' (compares with zero). dbt-23: change the (d) rationale to 'Deducts simple interest (10% x 2 years) instead of discounting' with trap wrong-rule.

issue: dbt-02 ('Using the previous facts...') and dbt-24 ('Using the note above...') refer to other items. Practice sets are shuffled, so 'previous' or 'above' may point to nothing. Each stem also prints the key of its partner item ($171,468 is dbt-01's key; $82,645 is dbt-23's key), so whichever item comes second is cued.
evidence: src/lib/quiz.ts lines 84-98 and 114-135 shuffle and interleave practice items. dbt-02 stem: 'note recorded at $171,468; 8%' = dbt-01 key (c). dbt-24 stem: 'recorded at $82,645 at 10%' = dbt-23 key (c).
source: Review brief section 2, answer cues: one item revealing the answer to another
fix: Make dbt-02 and dbt-24 standalone, with different numbers and without the partner's PV. Better, turn each into a two-step item: e.g. 'On 1/1 Year 1, a $150,000 noninterest-bearing note due in 2 years is issued for land; market rate 7%. What is the note's carrying amount at 12/31 Year 1?' (131,016 x 1.07 = 140,187). Alternatively, fold each pair into one item.

issue: Near-duplicates within the module. dbt-23/dbt-24 repeat dbt-01/dbt-02 (a 2-year noninterest-bearing note at present value, then Year-1 effective interest). Together with the lesson's worked example, that one computation is tested 3 times. dbt-22 repeats dbt-16 (settle debt with land: land gain = FV - carrying; restructuring gain = debt - FV). Meanwhile the module never tests a note with an unreasonably low stated rate, Year-2 interest or carrying amount, an equity-for-debt TDR, or a TDR loss on an asset transfer.
source: Review brief section 2 item 7 (duplicates)
fix: Replace dbt-23/24 with (i) a note with an unreasonably low stated rate (e.g. a $100,000, 2% three-year note when the market rate is 10%: PV = 100,000 x 0.75131 + 2,000 x 2.48685 = 80,105) and (ii) the carrying amount at the end of Year 2. Replace dbt-22 with a TDR settled by granting equity (FV of the shares vs carrying amount of the debt; par and APIC) or with land whose FV is below its carrying amount (a loss on the asset plus a restructuring gain).

issue: Gain or loss on extinguishment (net carrying amount vs reacquisition price, reported in income) is tested the same way in 5 MCQs, plus the lesson's faded example and flashcard fc4. far-x2-32 is a near-copy of far-dbt-chk2 and a subset of far-x2-16: both exam items use a $980,000 carrying amount. Both also sit on the same mock (far-mock-3), so one cues the other and that mock tests the same fact twice.
source: Review brief section 2 item 7; ASC 470-50-40-2
fix: Rewrite far-x2-32 for an untested angle, e.g. a call at a premium that must update discount amortization to the call date first; reacquisition costs; the 10% modification test with lender fees; or the debtor TDR undiscounted test. Or at least swap it off far-mock-3 for another in-scope Area II item.

issue: Cross-module duplicates. dbt-15 is the same question as far-bond-15 (after ASU 2020-06, convertible bonds with no derivative are recorded entirely as debt). dbt-19 tests the same book-value conversion rule as far-bond-26. dbt-14 is the same relative-fair-value warrant allocation as far-bond-27. dbt-pre1 is the same fact pattern and answer as far-bse-21 and far-x1-28 (short-term note refinanced long-term after year-end, before issuance, is noncurrent).
evidence: far-bond-15 stem: 'After ASU 2020-06, how does an issuer generally account for convertible bonds with no derivative features?', key 'Entirely as debt'. far-bond-27: detachable warrants, relative FV (103,000 x 8/104 = 7,923). far-bond-26: book value method on conversion. far-bse-21 / far-x1-28: refinancing completed before issuance, key noncurrent.
source: Review brief section 2 item 7
fix: Keep convertibles and warrants in one module, next to the new lesson section. Vary the duplicates: e.g. dbt-15 could test convertible debt issued at a substantial premium (premium to APIC, ASC 470-20-25-13), and dbt-19 could test an induced conversion (ASU 2024-04, testable 2026: expense equals the FV of the sweetener). Make dbt-pre1 a refinancing via issuance of equity securities, or one where the post-year-end bond issue is smaller than the note.

issue: Answer cue. In dbt-03, dbt-06 and dbt-09 the key is the bare one-word option 'Current', while every distractor carries a qualifier or justification ('Noncurrent, because...', 'Current only to the extent...', 'Noncurrent if...'). Across the module, 'Current' is the key in 5 of the 7 classification items. In dbt-22 the key is the only two-part option; the distractors say 'only' or 'no gain'.
evidence: cues.md flags 'key much shortest' for dbt-03, 06, 09, 25 and 28, and 'key longest; absolutes only in distractors a,c,d' for dbt-22. Keys: dbt-03 'Current'; dbt-06 'Current'; dbt-09 'Current'; dbt-25 'Current'; dbt-28 'Current'.
source: Review brief section 2 item 6
fix: Give the keys parallel justifications, e.g. dbt-03 'Current, because it was repaid with current assets before the refinancing'; dbt-06 'Current, in full, because the lender can demand repayment'; dbt-09 'Current, because the ability to refinance was not demonstrated'. For dbt-22, add a reversed two-part distractor ('$20,000 restructuring gain; $30,000 asset gain').

issue: Implausible distractors that no prepared candidate would pick, leaving 2-3 live options. Examples: 'As equity' (dbt-18 d, dbt-28 c), 'The trust is treated as equity' (dbt-26 d), 'As a reduction of equity' (dbt-27 d), 'The names of all bondholders' (dbt-05 c), '$110,000' and '$0' for a note bought with $90,000 of equipment (dbt-17 c, d), 'Split 50/50' (pre1 b).
evidence: None of these models a misconception taught or commonly held. Their explanations are one-liners ('It remains a liability.', 'Not the treatment.', 'Not equity costs.', 'A liability exists.').
source: Review brief section 2 item 2 and item 8 (realism)
fix: Replace each with a misconception-based option. dbt-18 (d): 'Current, with disclosure of the grace period'. dbt-28 (c): 'Current only if the lender accelerates before the statements are issued'. dbt-26 (d): 'The bonds and trust assets are offset and the net shown'. dbt-27 (d): 'Deferred and recognized only when the line is first drawn'. dbt-05 (c): 'The fair value of the debt for all entities'. dbt-17 (c): '$100,000 with interest imputed at the market rate'. pre1 (b): 'Current, with the refinancing disclosed'.

issue: Thin or circular explanations. In the computational items dbt-16, dbt-21 and dbt-22, neither the item explanation nor the key explanation shows any numbers. Several distractor rationales just restate that the option is wrong.
evidence: dbt-16 key: 'Correct. The land is first remeasured.' (no 450-350 = 100,000 or 600-450 = 150,000). dbt-21 key: 'Correct. Future cash flows are below the carrying amount.' (no 110,000-90,000). dbt-22 key: 'Correct. Both gains are recognized.' (no 70-50, 100-70). dbt-17 never mentions the $10,000 discount or that it becomes interest. Distractors: dbt-23 (a) 'Impute interest.', (d) 'Not the computation.'; dbt-26 (c) 'Not extinguished.', (d) 'Not the treatment.'; dbt-19 (b) 'Not for conversion.'; dbt-27 (d) 'Not equity costs.'; dbt-25 (c) 'That is not permitted.'
source: Review brief section 2 item 4
fix: Add the computation to each key explanation and to the item explanation, e.g. dbt-16: 'Gain on land = 450,000 - 350,000 = 100,000; gain on restructuring = 600,000 - 450,000 = 150,000 (ASC 470-60-35-3).' dbt-21: '110,000 - 90,000 = 20,000 gain; the debt is carried at 90,000 and every later payment reduces principal; no interest expense.' Have each distractor rationale name the error it models.

issue: Four trap labels don't match the misconception their distractors model.
evidence: dbt-10 (d) 'Equity increases' is labeled irrelevant-fact, but the stem has no irrelevant fact; the error is wrong-rule. dbt-14 (c) $10,000 is labeled wrong-classification, but it is the incremental (residual) method, i.e. wrong-rule: 1,000,000 - 990,000. dbt-21 (b) 'No gain; reduce future interest' is labeled wrong-classification, but it applies the wrong branch of the 470-60 test, i.e. wrong-rule. dbt-24 (b) $17,355 is labeled wrong-classification, but it takes the whole discount (100,000 - 82,645) in Year 1, i.e. wrong-period.
source: src/content/schema.ts TRAP_TYPES
fix: Relabel: dbt-10 (d) wrong-rule; dbt-14 (c) wrong-rule; dbt-21 (b) wrong-rule; dbt-24 (b) wrong-period.

issue: The stem says only 'A debtor settles $100,000 of debt by transferring land'. It never states financial difficulty or a creditor concession, yet the key reads '$30,000 TDR gain' and the explanation calls it a restructuring. Without those facts the transaction is an ordinary extinguishment under 470-50 (same numbers, different label), so the key asserts a classification the stem doesn't support.
evidence: Compare dbt-16 ('A debtor in difficulty settles...') and dbt-13 ('A debtor in financial difficulty...'). The numbers are the same either way: 100,000 - 70,000 = 30,000 gain on settlement; 70,000 - 50,000 = 20,000 gain on the land.
source: ASC 470-60-15-5 (TDR = financial difficulty + concession); ASC 470-50-40-2
fix: Add 'A debtor in financial difficulty... the creditor accepts land in full settlement' to the stem, or change the key text to '$30,000 gain on settlement of the debt; $20,000 gain on the land'.

issue: calc is true, but no computation is needed: the answer is the equipment's stated fair value ($90,000). The stem's 'At what amount is the note recorded?' could also be read as asking for the face amount (a gross-method note at $100,000 with a $10,000 discount).
evidence: Key (a) $90,000 = the fair value given in the stem; no arithmetic. Under the gross method, Notes payable is credited at 100,000 and Discount on notes payable is debited 10,000.
source: ASC 835-30-25-10; schema calc semantics (set only when a computation is needed)

issue: The lesson states the classification rules incompletely. (1) Refinancing: it omits that the entity must intend to refinance; that a post-balance-sheet issuance of equity securities also qualifies; and the conditions a financing agreement must meet (it doesn't expire or isn't callable within one year, it isn't cancelable by the lender, no violation exists, the lender is able to honor it). The lesson only says 'qualifying', and chk1 relies on those conditions in its stem. (2) Callable debt: the waiver must run 'for more than one year (or operating cycle, if longer)', but the lesson and takeaways drop the operating-cycle alternative. Flashcard fc2 has the same gaps.
evidence: Lesson: 'refinance it long-term, or sign a qualifying non-cancelable financing agreement'; takeaway: 'waives the right for more than one year'. ASC 470-10-45-14: intent plus ability demonstrated by (a) a post-BS-date issuance of a long-term obligation or equity securities, or (b) a financing agreement meeting 45-14(b)(1)-(3). ASC 470-10-45-11(a): 'for more than one year (or operating cycle, if longer)'. fc2 back: 'actual long-term refinancing or a qualifying financing agreement'.
fix: Add to the 'Refinancing traps' list: intent is required; equity securities also qualify; a qualifying agreement doesn't expire within one year, isn't cancelable by the lender, has no violations, and the lender can honor it; the noncurrent amount is capped at the amount available (a reasonable estimate of the minimum if it fluctuates). Add '(or operating cycle, if longer)' to the callable-debt rule. Update fc2 to match.

issue: Two defensible answers. The stem does not say how the excess of cost over par is allocated on retirement. ASC 505-30-30-8 allows two treatments: allocate it between APIC (capped at the pro-rata APIC of the same issue plus prior treasury gains) and retained earnings, or charge the whole excess over par to retained earnings. The second treatment gives distractor (a) $14,000, and its rationale ('Remove par and APIC first') wrongly calls a permitted method an error.
evidence: Retire 1,000 sh: cost 15,000; par 1,000; pro-rata APIC-common 1,000 x (10-1) = 9,000. Allocation method: RE = 15,000 - 1,000 - 9,000 = 5,000 (key b). Permitted alternative, 'charged entirely to retained earnings': RE = 15,000 - 1,000 = 14,000 = choice (a). Blind answer b, flagged as ambiguous.
source: ASC 505-30-30-8 (from APB 6 para 12a); PwC Viewpoint, Financing transactions guide sec. 9.4 'Share retirement' (https://viewpoint.pwc.com/dt/us/en/pwc/accounting_guides/financing_transactio/financing_transactio_US/chapter_9_share_repu_US/94_share_retirement_US.html) lists both the 'retained earnings only' and the 'split between APIC and RE' options

issue: Two defensible answers. The stem asks how the company 'may' treat shipping performed after control transfers (FOB shipping point). Without the policy election, that shipping is a promised service that is evaluated as a performance obligation, so (a) 'As a separate obligation' is also permitted. The key's rationale 'Not a separate obligation' states the election's result as the unconditional rule, and the qualifier 'by election' in the key alone cues it.
evidence: ASC 606-10-25-18B (added by ASU 2016-10): an entity that elects to treat shipping and handling after control transfers as a fulfillment activity accrues the cost. An entity that does not elect evaluates the shipping as a promised service (usually a separate performance obligation). Both (a) and (c) are therefore ways the company 'may' account for it. Choice (a)'s own rationale ('It may elect fulfillment-cost treatment') does not say why (a) is wrong.
fix: Reword the stem: 'A company ships goods FOB shipping point and arranges and pays for the freight. Which treatment does ASC 606 permit as an accounting policy election for the shipping?' Or state that the company has made the election and ask how the freight is accounted for. Change (c)'s rationale to 'Correct. With the election, shipping after control transfers is a fulfillment cost accrued when revenue is recognized.' Change (a)'s rationale to 'Without the election, shipping after control transfers is a promised service that may be a separate performance obligation. The question asks about the election.'

issue: A fact needed to answer is missing. The stem says the goods have already been shipped and the $5,000 deposit is nonrefundable, but it never says whether the company still has an obligation to transfer more goods. If the deposit relates to goods already transferred and the company has stopped transferring with no further obligation, ASC 606-10-25-7(c) allows $5,000 of revenue, so (a) becomes correct. Choice (a)'s rationale relies on a fact the stem does not give ('obligations remain').
evidence: ASC 606-10-25-7, as amended by ASU 2016-12, lists three events that allow consideration received to be recognized as revenue when Step 1 fails: (a) no remaining obligations and substantially all consideration received and nonrefundable; (b) contract terminated and consideration nonrefundable; (c) control of the goods to which the consideration relates has been transferred, the entity has stopped transferring and has no obligation to transfer more, and the consideration is nonrefundable. 'Ships goods' plus a 'nonrefundable deposit' puts the item in event (c) territory. The stem also says credit 'has deteriorated', which suggests a contract that existed earlier. Reassessment under 606-10-25-5 is prospective and does not reverse revenue already recognized.
fix: Reword: 'Before delivering any goods, a company receives a nonrefundable $5,000 deposit from a new customer. The company remains obligated to deliver the goods, but collection of substantially all of the remaining consideration is not probable. How is the deposit recorded?' Keep key (b). issue: The Step 1 paragraph on contracts that fail the criteria is incomplete. It omits the third event added by ASU 2016-12 (control of the related goods transferred, transfers stopped, no further obligation, and the consideration nonrefundable). It states 'the contract is terminated' without the requirement that the consideration be nonrefundable. It also never mentions reassessment when the customer's credit significantly deteriorates.
evidence: Lesson: 'cash received is recorded as a liability until they are met, the contract is terminated, or the entity has no remaining obligations and substantially all consideration is received and nonrefundable.' ASC 606-10-25-7(b) requires 'the contract has been terminated, and the consideration received from the customer is nonrefundable'. 606-10-25-7(c) is missing. 606-10-25-5 (reassessment after a significant change in facts, such as deteriorating credit) is not covered.
fix: Rewrite the sentence: 'Consideration received is a liability until (a) the criteria are later met, or one of these occurs with the consideration nonrefundable: (b) the entity has no remaining obligations and has received substantially all of the consideration; (c) the contract is terminated; or (d) the entity has transferred control of the goods the consideration relates to, has stopped transferring, and has no obligation to transfer more.' Add one line: 'Once a contract qualifies, it is reassessed only if facts change significantly (e.g., the customer's credit deteriorates sharply); the reassessment applies going forward.'

issue: Ten practice items (36% of the module's 28 practice MCQs) test ASC 606 rules that neither revenue lesson teaches: contract modifications, the shipping-and-handling election, bill-and-hold criteria, consignment revenue timing, repurchase agreements, customer-acceptance clauses, and functional vs. symbolic licenses. A learner who misses one is routed back to a lesson with no content on the rule.
evidence: I searched every FAR lesson. Contract modifications (rev1-12, -18, -22; ASC 606-10-25-10 to 25-13): no lesson teaches them; the only 'modif' hit in this lesson is 'significantly modified/customized' in the distinctness flowchart. Shipping-and-handling election (rev1-20; 25-18B): no lesson. Bill-and-hold criteria (rev1-14, -28; 55-81 to 55-84): only a one-row ownership table in far-inventory-cost, with no criteria. Consignment revenue timing (rev1-16; 55-79/80): only ownership in far-inventory-cost. Repurchase agreements (rev1-17; 55-66 to 55-78): no revenue lesson; far-leases-operating mentions repurchase options only for sale-leaseback. Customer acceptance (rev1-19; 55-85 to 55-88): far-revenue-measurement lists 'customer acceptance' only as a control indicator. Licenses of IP (rev1-15; 55-54 to 55-65): no revenue lesson.
fix: Add a short section to this lesson, 'Contract modifications and special arrangements'. It needs: (1) a modification decision table: a separate contract if distinct goods are added at SSP; otherwise prospective (terminate and create a new contract) if the remaining goods are distinct, or a cumulative catch-up if they are not; (2) the shipping-and-handling election; (3) a one-line rule each for consignment, bill-and-hold (four criteria), repurchase agreements (forward/call: below the original price is a lease, at or above it is financing; put option), customer acceptance (objective vs. subjective specifications), and licenses (functional = point in time; symbolic = over time). Add an inline check on modifications. Alternatively, move the Step 5 special-arrangement items to far-revenue-measurement and teach them there.

issue: Numeric distractor rationales read only 'Not the computation.' and never name the error that produces the number. Two distractors model no recognizable misconception. The item-level explanations for rev1-23, -24 and -26 give no computation.
evidence: I reproduced each distractor in python. rev1-21 (c) 55,000 = 100,000 − 20,000 − 25,000, the residual approach (equivalently, the whole 25,000 discount assigned to the equipment); its rationale is 'Not the computation.' rev1-21 (d) 75,000 = 100,000 − 25,000 (deducting only the support SSP), which is no principled error. rev1-23 (b) 450,000 = the amount remitted to airlines; rationale 'Not the computation.' rev1-24 (c) 90,000 = 100,000 × (1 − 2 × 5%), which is no modeled error. rev1-25 (c) 500,000 = 800,000 − 300,000, the estimated cost to complete; rationale 'Not the computation.' rev1-26 (d) 300,000 = costs incurred; rationale 'Not the computation.' rev1-26 (a) 15,000 = 50,000 × 300,000/1,000,000, a pro-rata loss using the price as the base; its rationale ('Recognize the entire loss') is adequate. issue: There is an answer cue, and the key's wording is imprecise. The stem asks 'Why is…?'. The three distractors begin 'Because…' and the key alone does not. Distractor (d) carries the only absolute ('all services are always'). The key's 'useful on its own' misstates the capable-of-being-distinct test: the maintenance is useful together with a readily available resource (the delivered machine), not on its own.
evidence: Choices: (a) 'Because it's performed over time…', (b) 'Because it's billed separately…', (c) 'It is useful on its own and isn't integrated with the machine', (d) 'Because all services are always separate obligations'. Choice (c)'s own rationale says 'useful with readily available resources — the delivered machine'. ASC 606-10-25-19(a) and 25-20.
fix: Make the grammar parallel: 'Because the customer can benefit from it together with the delivered machine, and it doesn't significantly modify or integrate with the machine.' Replace (d) with a plausible misconception, e.g., 'Because the maintenance has a longer term than the machine's warranty.'

issue: A fact is missing. The stem asks for the loss recognized 'this period' on a contract that 'now has' revised estimated costs. That implies earlier periods, but it doesn't say whether gross profit was recognized in them. Any profit recognized earlier must be reversed this period, so the period loss would exceed $50,000.
evidence: Total expected loss = 1,050,000 − 1,000,000 = 50,000. If, for example, 75,000 of gross profit had been recognized in a prior year (from rev1-25's estimates), the current-period loss would be 125,000 (ASC 605-35-25-46/47; cf. rev2-07, which states the prior profit). The key is correct only if this is the first period, or if no profit was recognized before.
fix: Add 'This is the first year of the contract (no gross profit has been recognized previously).' Or ask for 'the total loss recognized on the contract to date'. Add the computation to the explanation: '1,050,000 − 1,000,000 = 50,000 recognized in full immediately.'

In (b)'s rationale, name the error: 'Deducting the points' full SSP (a residual approach) isn't relative allocation.'

issue: The lesson's examples table says that selling a car with a 'standard 3-year manufacturer warranty' means the seller accrues the warranty cost. That holds only if the seller is the manufacturer. For a dealer or retailer, the manufacturer's warranty is not the seller's obligation at all. That is exactly the reasoning in lesson check far-rev1-chk2 ('The standard manufacturer warranty isn't a separate obligation of the retailer'). As written, the table and the check point different ways.

issue: The lesson, flashcard f5 and aud-rm-17 teach "clearly trivial" as a purely quantitative cut-off: anything below the threshold need not be accumulated. The module's own TBS aud-tbs-u3-risk-materiality (row qual.u3) correctly scores a $7,000 misstatement below the $8,000 threshold as "Accumulate and evaluate" because it lets the entity meet a debt covenant. A student who learned the rule from the lesson, card or MCQ will get that TBS row wrong.
evidence: Lesson takeaway (line 36): "Misstatements below the clearly trivial threshold need not be accumulated." f5 back: "Misstatements below it are clearly inconsequential, individually and in aggregate, and need not be accumulated." aud-rm-17 key "No" with explanation "misstatements that are clearly trivial needn't be accumulated", answering a stem about misstatements "below the clearly trivial threshold". AU-C 450.A2-A3: clearly trivial is judged "by any criteria of size, nature, or circumstances", and when there is any uncertainty the matter is treated as not clearly trivial. So an amount below the threshold is not automatically clearly trivial. TBS u3 qual.u3 key = "Accumulate and evaluate" ($7,000 < $8,000 CT, covenant effect).
source: AU-C 450.05, .A2-.A3 (confirmed via secondary sources: https://open-exam-prep.com/study-guides/cpa-aud/final-evaluation-documentation/evaluating-audit-findings-misstatements ; ISA 450.A2 https://is.muni.cz/el/econ/podzim2015/MPF_AAUD/um/60366355/ISA_450.pdf)
fix: Lesson takeaway: "Misstatements below the clearly trivial threshold need not be accumulated, unless their nature or circumstances (e.g., a covenant, fraud) make them more than inconsequential; if in doubt, accumulate." f5 back: add "unless qualitative factors (nature or circumstances) make them not clearly trivial". aud-rm-17: reword the stem to "...below the clearly trivial threshold, with no qualitative factors present?", or keep the stem and add the qualifier to the key explanation.

issue: Four single-fact recall items are labeled analysis or evaluation with difficulty 3. That is two to three skill levels too high. It inflates the module's analysis and evaluation counts, which feed the Blueprint skill-mix targets.
evidence: aud-rm-24 (analysis/3): "IR and CR both high -> detection risk must be low" is the same one-step relationship as aud-x2-38, which is labeled remembering/1. aud-rm-25 (analysis/3, calc:true): "PM $75,000 -> TM up to $75,000" only requires recalling TM <= PM; there is no computation. aud-rm-26 (evaluation/3): "RMM rises -> modify planned procedures" is recall of AU-C 315. aud-rm-27 (evaluation/3): "controls over a significant risk relied on -> test in the current period" is recall of AU-C 330.15. Blueprint definitions: Analysis = examining interrelationships to identify causes and support inferences; Evaluation = examining and judging the outcomes of analysis. None of these items requires either. Practice+exam mix as labeled: R11/A17/An4/E3 (31/49/11/9%). As corrected by this review (this finding plus the one-level mislabels): R20/A14/An0/E1 (57/40/0/3%). The Blueprint ranges are R&U 30-40, App 30-40, An 15-25, Eval 5-15.
source: AICPA 2026 Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill definitions and AUD skill allocation (review/reference/blueprint-notes.md); AU-C 315; AU-C 330.15; AU-C 530.A11
fix: Relabel aud-rm-24, -25, -26 and -27 as skill remembering, difficulty 1, and set calc:false on aud-rm-25. issue: The big-idea definition of materiality ("the size or nature of misstatement that would change a reasonable user's decisions") is looser than the current AU-C 320 description. SAS 138 aligned that description with the U.S. judicial "substantial likelihood ... influence the judgment of a reasonable user" standard.
evidence: Lesson line 19-20. After SAS 138 (effective for periods ending on or after Dec 15, 2020), AU-C 320.02 reads approximately: misstatements are material "if there is a substantial likelihood that, individually or in the aggregate, they would influence the judgment made by a reasonable user based on the financial statements". "Would change decisions" overstates the threshold. This is exam-testable wording.
source: SAS 138, Amendments to the Description of the Concept of Materiality (AICPA: https://www.aicpa-cima.com/resources/download/aicpa-statement-on-auditing-standards-no-138, which says SAS 138 aligns the description with the U.S. judicial system's); AU-C 320.02
fix: Change it to: "Materiality defines 'materially wrong': misstatements (including omissions) are material if there is a substantial likelihood that, individually or in aggregate, they would influence the judgment of a reasonable user (AU-C 320, as amended by SAS 138)."

issue: The variable-consideration constraint is stated backwards in strength. Lesson keyTakeaway (line 31: 'constrained to the amount for which a significant reversal is not probable'), lesson Step 3 table (line 49: 'include only to the extent a significant reversal is not probable'), flashcard far-rev2-fc2 ('Include only the amount for which a significant revenue reversal is not probable'), the far-rev2-01 stem ('concludes a significant reversal is not probable') and the far-x3-04 explanation ('asks whether a significant reversal is probable') all use 'a reversal is not probable'. ASC 606 requires that it be PROBABLE THAT a significant reversal will NOT occur, which is a much higher bar.
evidence: 'Reversal not probable' is satisfied whenever the chance of reversal is below the 'probable' (likely-to-occur, roughly 70-75%) threshold; 'probable that no reversal will occur' needs roughly 70-75%+ confidence of NO reversal. Worked case (far-rev2-21 facts): a $10,000 all-or-nothing bonus with 60% chance of being earned. Under the platform's wording the 40% chance of a full reversal is 'not probable', so $10,000 is included; under ASC 606-10-32-11 it is not probable (only 60%) that a reversal will not occur, so the bonus is constrained (likely to $0). A student applying the lesson's rule gets this exam-style question wrong. Grep shows the wording is consistent across lesson, flashcard and items, so the error is systematic, not a typo.
source: ASC 606-10-32-11 ('only to the extent that it is probable that a significant reversal in the amount of cumulative revenue recognized will not occur when the uncertainty ... is subsequently resolved'); ASC 606-10-32-12 (factors)
fix: Reword everywhere to 'include variable consideration only to the extent it is probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue will NOT occur when the uncertainty is resolved'. far-rev2-01 stem: 'concludes it is probable that including the bonus will not result in a significant revenue reversal'. far-x3-04 explanation: 'The constraint then asks whether it is probable that a significant reversal will not occur; the stem says the constraint does not limit the amount.' Consider adding one lesson sentence and a check item showing a 60% binary bonus being constrained.

issue: Dropdown row d2 (Installation) is keyed 'Point in time' because it is 'a short, routine service completed on October 1'. Duration is not a criterion. Installation performed on equipment the customer already controls (control passed on delivery the same day) meets the over-time criterion of ASC 606-10-25-27(b). A candidate who answers 'Over time' applies the standard correctly and is scored wrong.
evidence: 606-10-25-27(b): over time if the entity's performance creates or enhances an asset that the customer controls as it is enhanced. The exhibit says the equipment was delivered (control transferred) and installed on Oct 1, and that installation is distinct and routine, so the customer controls the asset being enhanced. Many textbooks simplify one-day installation to 'recognized when complete'. Both answers are therefore defensible, and the revenue amount (90,000 in Year 1) is identical under either. The row tests an ambiguous classification and scores one defensible answer as wrong (1 of 8 cells = 12.5% of the TBS).
fix: Either (1) delete row d2, (2) change the facts so the answer is unambiguous (e.g., installation performed over November-December on customer-owned equipment -> Over time, and update Year-1 revenue accordingly), or (3) accept both options. If kept, replace the explanation with a criterion-based one ('the customer controls the equipment being installed -> over time; here performance is completed on October 1, so all 90,000 is recognized that day').

issue: Distractor (b) $50,000 is explained as 'This recognizes only the proportional loss' (trap wrong-rule). That is not what produces $50,000. $50,000 is the 200,000 expected loss netted against (instead of added to) the 150,000 prior profit, a sign error. The proportional-loss error produces a different number.
evidence: Python: total loss = 3,200,000 - 3,000,000 = 200,000; progress = 2,400,000/3,200,000 = 75%. Proportional cumulative loss = 75% x 200,000 = 150,000 -> Year-2 loss = 150,000 + 150,000 = 300,000 (not an option). 200,000 - 150,000 = 50,000 = (b). Note (d) $150,000 is both 'only reverses prior profit' and the proportional cumulative loss.
fix: Rewrite (b)'s explanation: 'This nets the 150,000 prior profit against the 200,000 loss; prior profit must be reversed in addition to recognizing the full loss' (trap: reversed). Optionally replace (d) with $300,000 ('recognizes the loss only in proportion to progress, 75% x 200,000 + 150,000'), trap wrong-rule.

issue: Distractor (a) '$30,000, in proportion to progress' cannot be derived from the stem, which gives no costs incurred or percent complete. The trap models a real misconception (spreading the loss by progress), but the number is arbitrary, so it reads as a guess, not a computable error.
evidence: Stem: price 1,000,000; estimated total costs 1,100,000; no Year-1 costs. 30,000 = 30% x 100,000 needs a 30% progress figure (costs to date 330,000) that is not given.
fix: Add 'Costs incurred to date are $330,000' to the stem so (a) = 330,000/1,100,000 x 100,000 = 30,000 models the proportional error. Or change (a) to a number derivable from the stem.

issue: The explanations don't teach the computation or the rule's conditions, and two distractor rationales are wrong. Item explanation: 'A discount is allocated to specific obligations when there's observable evidence it relates to them' (no numbers, no criteria). (b) $30 'Not the computation.' (trap distractor-number), but $30 = 40 - 10 models allocating the entire $10 discount to A. (c) $50 'A gets its standalone price.' — A's SSP is $40, so the rationale is confusing and $50 models nothing. The stem also omits that each product is regularly sold separately (criterion (a) of 606-10-32-37).
evidence: Python: total SSP 40+25+45 = 110; discount 10. B+C SSP = 70, regularly sold for 60 -> discount 10 = the whole contract discount -> all to B and C, A = 40. Proportional: 40/110 x 100 = 36.36 = (a). 40 - 10 = 30 = (b).
fix: Item explanation: 'Total SSP 110 vs price 100 -> 10 discount. A, B and C are each regularly sold separately, and B+C are regularly sold together for 60 (a 10 discount on their 70 SSP), which matches the contract discount, so the entire discount goes to B and C (ASC 606-10-32-37). A = 40; B+C share 60.' (b): 'Assigns the entire discount to A (40 - 10)'; trap wrong-rule. Replace (c) with a modeled error (e.g., $45.45 = 50/110 x 100) or rewrite its rationale. issue: The stem omits facts needed to value the material right. (1) The product's standalone selling price is not stated (the key assumes the $1,000 sale price). evidence: ASC 606-10-55-44 measures the option's SSP at the discount the customer would obtain, adjusted for any discount available without the option and for the likelihood of exercise. The ASC illustration of a discount voucher (Example 49) uses a 40% voucher 'up to' a cap with a separately estimated average purchase below the cap, and a 10% discount available to all customers. Applying that structure here (e.g., average purchase $400, 10% general discount) gives voucher SSP = 400 x 30% x 80% = 96 and product = 1,000 x 1,000/1,096 = 912, not 862. The key is reachable only by assuming facts the stem doesn't give.
